metadata.title: Blow up for the critical gKdV equation III: exotic regimes

extraction_notes.note: Restated copies of the tail definitions, eqs. (1.13)-(1.14) in the strategy section and (A.1)-(A.3) in Appendix A, get no node (none is cited); the Section 2.2 versions DP11/DP12 with (2.14)-(2.16) are kept.

The proof of Theorem 1.1 is split between step (iv) of Section 1.4 (PP2) and one sentence in Section 3.1 (PP6); the proof of Proposition 3.1 runs across Sections 3.1-3.5, so it is split into PP7 (setup by contradiction) and PP11 (topological conclusion), with the intermediate bounds (BS2'), (BS3') as separate claims with their own proofs.

The bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS3), (BS2'), (BS3') are \leqno-tagged unnumbered displays cited by name only; they stay inside the proposition and claim nodes, and references to them became hand-added uses edges.
Numbered equation (1.3) is named the sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a citation, so it is a theorem (external) rather than an equation.

Uncited standard facts about gKdV (conservation laws, symmetries, global existence below the mass of Q) typed claim with origin external; ClP1 also introduces M and E but is kept a claim rather than a definition.

The strategy section derives the formal dynamics in prose; the decomposition ansatz and the explicit threshold solution are claims, the formal modulation system is a heuristic claim, and the formal integration is a prose proof of ClP6.

The opening sentence 'We now claim from a standard topological argument ...' matches the inline-claim opener, but its argument is the whole remaining section; it is a setup step instead of a parent of every later step.

metadata.extraction_comment: Lemma 2.1 (LP1) is kept origin paper although its part (ii) is quoted from MMR1; Lemma 2.2 (LP2) and the localized virial Lemma B.1 (LP6) are marked external (MMR1) as the paper says it recalls them.

nodes.name: Eq. (1.1): L2-critical gKdV Cauchy problem
nodes.statement: {\rm (gKdV)}\quad \left\{\begin{array}{ll} u_t + (u_{xx} + u^5)_x =0, \quad & (t,x)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}, \\ u(0,x)= u_0(x), & x\in {\mathbb R}. \end{array} \right.
nodes.label: kdv

nodes.name: Eq. (1.2): Soliton profile Q and its rescaling
nodes.statement: Q_\lambda(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12} }Q \left(\frac x\lambda\right) ,\quad Q(x) = \left(\frac {3}{\cosh^{2}\left( 2 x\right)}\right)^{\frac14}, \quad Q''+Q^5 =Q.
nodes.label: eq:Q

nodes.name: Eq. (1.4): Slightly supercritical mass condition
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.label: utwosmall

nodes.name: Eq. (1.5): Negative energy initial data class
nodes.statement: \hbox {$u_0 \in H^1$ such that \eqref{utwosmall} and $E(u_0)<0$.}
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.label: classe

nodes.name: Eq. (1.6): Blow up rate of the minimal mass solution S
nodes.statement: \| S_x(t)\|_{L^2}\sim \frac{\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{ t}\ \ \mbox{as} \ t\downarrow 0.
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.label: th1:1.4

nodes.name: Eq. (1.7): Stable blow up rate in A
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \frac {\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{\ell_0 (T-t)} \quad \hbox{as $t\uparrow T$ for some $\ell_0>0$.}
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.label: papI1

nodes.name: Eq. (1.8): Displayed estimate
nodes.statement: u(t, \cdot +x(t))\to Q_{\lambda_\infty} \hbox{ in $H^1_{\rm loc}$ as $t\to +\infty$ for $|\lambda_\infty-1| + |x'(t)-1|\lesssim \delta(\alpha_0)$},
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$

nodes.name: Eq. (1.9): Finite time blow up rate t^{-nu}
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim t^{-\nu}\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\downarrow 0^+.
nodes.label: th:1:1

nodes.name: Eq. (1.10): Exponential grow up rate
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim e^{t} \ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\to +\infty.
nodes.label: th:1:4

nodes.name: Eq. (1.11): Power grow up rate t^nu
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim t^{\nu}\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\to +\infty.
nodes.label: th:1:5

nodes.name: Eq. (1.15): Decomposition ansatz with tail correction
nodes.statement: u(t,x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + \lambda^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,x(t)) Y_0 + \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x)
nodes.label: uu

nodes.name: Eq. (1.16): Renormalized time ds/dt
nodes.statement: \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}.
nodes.label: sharpintro

nodes.name: Eq. (1.17): Formal modulation system with tail
nodes.statement: \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left( \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right)=0.
nodes.label: dynsyst

nodes.name: Eq. (1.18): Unperturbed modulation system
nodes.statement: \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}, \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2}\right) =0,
nodes.label: dynsystbis

nodes.name: Eq. (1.19): Displayed estimate
nodes.statement: \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}=0,

nodes.name: Eq. (1.20): Explicit threshold solution of the formal system
nodes.statement: \lambda(s) = s^{-\beta}, \quad x(s) = \frac 1{1-\beta} s^{1-\beta},\quad b(s) =\frac {\beta}s.
nodes.label: eq:blx

nodes.name: Eq. (1.22): Heuristic Lyapunov monotonicity
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{ds}\left\{s^j {\mathcal F}\right\}+ s^j \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2 \lesssim s^{j-4}, \ \ j\geq 0.
nodes.label: cnkneneoe

nodes.name: Eq. (2.1): Exponential decay class Y
nodes.statement: \forall k\in \mathbb{N},\ \exists C_k,\, r_k>0,\ \forall y\in {{\mathbb R}},\quad |f^{(k)}(y)|\leq C_k (1+|y|)^{r_k} {e^{-|y|}},
nodes.label: Y

nodes.name: Eq. (2.2): Equation and normalization of Y_0
nodes.statement: L Y_0= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,Y_0)=-\frac 34 \int Q .
nodes.label: YQ

nodes.name: Eq. (2.3): Equation and limits of P
nodes.statement: (L P)'={\Lambda} Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to -\infty} P(y) = \frac 12 \int Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to +\infty} P(y) =0,
nodes.label: eq:23

nodes.name: Eq. (2.4): Scalar products of P with Q and Q'
nodes.statement: (P, Q) = \frac 1{16} \left(\int Q\right)^2 > 0,\quad (P, Q')=0.
nodes.label: PQ

nodes.name: Eq. (2.5): Cut-off chi_b
nodes.statement: \chi_b(y)= \chi\left(|b|^{\gamma} {y} \right),\ \ \gamma = \frac 34.
nodes.label: defgamma

nodes.name: Eq. (2.6): Definition of Q_b
nodes.statement: \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y).
nodes.label: eq:210

nodes.name: Eq. (2.7): Pointwise estimates on Q_b
nodes.statement: & |Q_b(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| \left( {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,0]}(|b|^\gamma y) + e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \\ & |Q_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} +|b|^{1+k \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,-1]}(|b|^\gamma y),\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}.
nodes.label: eq:001

nodes.name: Eq. (2.9): Definition of Psi_b
nodes.statement: -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b,
nodes.label: eq:201

nodes.name: Eq. (2.10): Estimates on Psi_b
nodes.statement: & |\Psi_b(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 \left(e^{-\frac {|y|} 2}+ {\mathbf{1}}_{[- 2,0]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) \right), \\ & |\Psi_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ (k+1) \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 e^{-\frac {|y|} 2} ,\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}.
nodes.label: eq:202

nodes.name: Eq. (2.12): Mass and energy of Q_b
nodes.statement: & \left|\int Q_b^2 - \left( \int Q^2 + 2b \int PQ \right)\right| \lesssim |b|^{2-\gamma}, \\ & \left| E(Q_b) + b \int PQ\right|\lesssim b^2 .
nodes.label: eq:204

nodes.name: Eq. (2.14): Tail initial data f_0
nodes.statement: f_0(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}c_0 x^{-\theta} & \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\\ 0 & \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$,}\end{array}\right.
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: deffz

nodes.name: Eq. (2.15): Derivative bounds for f_0
nodes.statement: \left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim |x|^{-\theta - k}, \ \ \forall (x,k)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{N}.
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: estfz

nodes.name: Eq. (2.16): gKdV flow of the tail q_0
nodes.statement: \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad q_0(0,x)= f_0(x).
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: defqz

nodes.name: Eq. (2.17): Tail propagation estimate
nodes.statement: \forall k\geq 0,\quad |\partial_x^k q_0(t,x) -f_0^{(k)}(x) | \lesssim t^{\frac 38} x^{-\theta-\frac {19}8 - k } \lesssim x^{-\theta-2 - k },
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: leqz3

nodes.name: Eq. (2.18): Time derivative bound for q_0
nodes.statement: |\partial_tq_0(t,x) | \lesssim x^{-\theta-3} .
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: leqz4

nodes.name: Eq. (2.19): Definition of w = u - q_0
nodes.label: defw

nodes.name: Eq. (2.20): Rough decomposition of w
nodes.statement: \forall t\in [0,t_0], \ \ & \lambda_1(t)<\frac {10}9 \lambda_0,\quad x_1(t)> \frac 9{10} x_0, \\ & w(t,x)=\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}_1(t)}(Q+\varepsilon_1)\left(t,\frac{x-x_1(t)}{\lambda_1(t)}\right)
nodes.label: decompo0

nodes.name: Eq. (2.22): Smallness of epsilon_1
nodes.statement: \forall t\in [0,t_0],\ \ \|\varepsilon_1(t)\|_{L^2}+\left(\int (\partial_y \varepsilon_1)^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} dy \right)^{\frac 12}\leq \alpha^*
nodes.label: hypeprochien

nodes.name: Eq. (2.23): Modulated decomposition
nodes.statement: \forall t\in [0,t_0],\quad {\lambda}^{\frac 12}(t) w(t,{\lambda}(t) y + x(t)) = Q_{{b}(t)}(y) +p(t) Y_0(y) +\varepsilon(t,y),
nodes.label: defofeps

nodes.name: Eq. (2.24): Definition of p and q
nodes.statement: p(t)= q(t,0),\quad q(t,y) = \lambda^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,\lambda(t) y +x(t)),
nodes.label: defp

nodes.name: Eq. (2.25): Orthogonality conditions
nodes.statement: (\varepsilon(t), y {\Lambda} Q )=(\varepsilon(t),\Lambda Q) =(\varepsilon(t),Q)=0,
nodes.label: ortho1

nodes.name: Eq. (2.26): Bounds on lambda and x
nodes.statement: \lambda(t)<\frac 54 \lambda_0,\quad x(t)>\frac 45 x_0.
nodes.label: lambdax

nodes.name: Eq. (2.27): L2 bound from mass conservation
nodes.statement: \|\varepsilon(s)\|^2_{L^2}\lesssim \left|\int u_0^2-\int Q^2\right| + |b(s)| +|p(s)| + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},
nodes.label: twobound

nodes.name: Eq. (2.28): H1 bound from energy conservation
nodes.statement: \frac 1{\lambda^2}\| \varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac b{\lambda^2} {+} c_0 \frac 4{\int Q}\lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right| + \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+ \frac { |p| }{x^2} + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x} + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} .
nodes.label: energbound

nodes.name: Eq. (2.29): Lower bound on x(t)
nodes.statement: \forall t\in [0,t_0],\quad x(t) > \frac 23 t + \frac 23 {x_0}.
nodes.label: surX

nodes.name: Eq. (2.30): Rescaled time s
nodes.statement: {s}=s(t)= s_0+ \int_{0}^{t} \frac {dt'}{{\lambda}^3(t')} \quad \text{or equivalently}\quad \frac {d{s}}{dt} = \frac 1{{\lambda}^3},\quad s(0)=s_0.
nodes.label: rescaledtime

nodes.name: Eq. (2.31): Modulation equations
nodes.statement: & \left|\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{\lambda} + {b}\right|+\left| \frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} - 1 \right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + b^2 +p^2 + \frac \lambda x |p|, \\ & |{b}_{s}| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}+|p| \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12}+|b|^2+ |b| |p| +p^4 + \frac \lambda x |p| ,\\ & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right) \right| \\ & \lesssim \frac 1{\lambda^2} \left( |b|^3+|p|^3 + (|b|+|p|)\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| \right). \nonumber
nodes.label: eq:2002bis

nodes.name: Eq. (2.34): Decomposition of u
nodes.statement: u(t,x) & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \\ & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right).
nodes.label: dec:2

nodes.name: Eq. (2.38): Equation of epsilon_Y
nodes.statement: \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon_Y & = (-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon_Y + \varepsilon_Y - (\varepsilon_Y+Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5)_y - (5 Q^4 q)_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon_Y \\ & + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b + \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon_Y)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y,
nodes.label: eqofepsY

nodes.name: Eq. (2.39): Equation of epsilon
nodes.statement: \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon - (\varepsilon +p Y_0 +Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5 + p5Q^4 Y_0\right)_y \\ & -p_s Y_0 +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} (\Lambda \varepsilon+p\Lambda Y_0) + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p Y_0)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y,
nodes.label: eqofeps

nodes.name: Eq. (2.40): Estimates on q
nodes.statement: \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad \|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \lambda(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad \|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}.
nodes.label: L2H1q

nodes.name: Eq. (2.41): Approximation of p
nodes.statement: \left|p(s) - c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|,
nodes.label: cl.1bis

nodes.name: Eq. (2.42): Localized bound on p - q
nodes.statement: e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| \lesssim \frac {\lambda(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} ,
nodes.label: cl.2

nodes.name: Eq. (2.43): Leading tail interaction term
nodes.statement: \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| \lesssim \frac {\lambda^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\lambda(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|,
nodes.label: cl.4bis

nodes.name: Eq. (2.44): Equation for p_s
nodes.statement: \left| p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}|p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right),
nodes.label: cl.2bis

nodes.name: Eq. (2.45): Bound on p_s
nodes.statement: |p_s| \lesssim \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right).
nodes.label: cl.2tri

nodes.name: Eq. (2.46): Bound on W - tilde W
nodes.statement: \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| ,
nodes.label: cl.3

nodes.name: Eq. (2.47): Projections of tilde W
nodes.statement: |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p| +|p| \left(\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} ,
nodes.label: cl.4

nodes.name: Eq. (2.48): Projection of tilde W on y Lambda Q
nodes.statement: |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2.
nodes.label: cl.5

nodes.name: Eq. (2.49): Estimate of p - q
nodes.statement:
& e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}.
nodes.label: pmq

nodes.name: Eq. (2.50): Refined b_s equation
nodes.statement: &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q) - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) \nonumber\\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right] + c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\bigg|\\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} +\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|.
nodes.label: eq:bautre

nodes.name: Eq. (2.53): Tail contribution to b_s
nodes.statement: & \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\nonumber \\ & = \frac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +\frac \theta 3 \frac {x_s}{x} \right) +O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|\right) + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\right).
nodes.label: pascancel

nodes.name: Eq. (2.54): Final b_s equation
nodes.statement: &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + \theta \frac {x_s}{x} \right) \bigg| \nonumber \\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| .
nodes.label: eq:b

nodes.name: Eq. (3.1): Choice of c_0
nodes.statement: c_0=-\frac {\int Q}2(\theta-1)(2\theta-1)^{\theta-1}.
nodes.label: defcobeta

nodes.name: Eq. (3.2): Weight functions phi_i
nodes.statement: \varphi_i(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{lll}e^{y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1+y \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ -\frac 12<y<\frac 12,\\ y^i\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>2, \end{array}\right. \ \ \varphi_i'(y) >0, \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R},
nodes.label: defphi1bis

nodes.name: Eq. (3.3): Weight function psi
nodes.statement: \psi(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} e^{2y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1 \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>-\tfrac 12,\end{array}\right. \ \ \psi'(y) \geq 0 \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}.
nodes.label: defphi2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.4): Weighted norm N_i
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{N}_i} (s) = \int \varepsilon_y^2(s,y) \psi_{B}(y)dy + \int \varepsilon^2(s,y) \varphi_{i,B}(y) dy,
nodes.label: eq:no

nodes.name: Eq. (3.5): Local norm N_{i,loc}
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}} (s) = \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi'_{i,B} (y) dy,\quad i=1,2.
nodes.label: eq:noloc

nodes.name: Eq. (3.7): Smallness and orthogonality of epsilon_0
nodes.statement: s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \varepsilon^2_0(y) dy+\|\varepsilon_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\varepsilon_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\varepsilon_0,\Lambda Q) =(\varepsilon_0,Q)=0.
nodes.label: A2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.8): Set D of initial parameters
nodes.statement: (\lambda_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\lambda,b) \ : \ | \lambda - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\},
nodes.label: estimation2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.9): Initial data u_0
nodes.statement: u_0(x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \lambda^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) Y_0+ \varepsilon_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\lambda_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x)
nodes.label: defu0

nodes.name: Eq. (3.10): Sharp asymptotics of x, lambda, b
nodes.statement: \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}},
nodes.label: sharp

nodes.name: Eq. (3.11): Bound on epsilon in H1
nodes.statement: \lambda^{-1} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}+ \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim 1.
nodes.label: sharpe

nodes.name: Eq. (3.12): Bounds on p and lambda/x
nodes.statement: 0< -p(s) \lesssim \frac 1 s,\quad \frac {\lambda}{x} \lesssim \frac 1 s,
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSp

nodes.name: Eq. (3.13): Modulation bounds under bootstrap
nodes.statement: \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right| + \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2},
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSlsl

nodes.name: Eq. (3.14): Bounds on lambda_s/lambda and x_s
nodes.statement: \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \right| \lesssim \frac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12},\quad \left| x_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\beta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} \right) ,
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSparam

nodes.name: Eq. (3.15): Bounds on b_s and p_s
nodes.statement: |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac 1{s^2},
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSbsps

nodes.name: Eq. (3.16): Bound on d/ds of b/lambda^2 + tail term
nodes.statement: & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2} +\frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right) \right| \nonumber \\ &\lesssim \frac 1{\lambda^2} \left( \frac 1{s^{\frac {29}{10}}} + \frac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}\right).
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSfond

nodes.name: Eq. (3.17): Conservation-law bounds on epsilon
nodes.statement: &\|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2\right|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\\ & \frac 1{\lambda^2} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{- \frac 1{10}} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} .
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSeps

nodes.name: Eq. (3.19): Tail monotonicity
nodes.statement: {\lambda^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\lambda^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}.
nodes.label: keyestimate

nodes.name: Eq. (3.20): Energy-virial functional F_i
nodes.statement: {\mathcal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \\ &- \frac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\right)\right)\psi_B\Big] .\nonumber
nodes.label: feps

nodes.name: Eq. (3.21): Lyapunov control
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} .
nodes.label: lyapounovconrolbis

nodes.name: Eq. (3.22): Coercivity of F_i
nodes.statement: -\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .
nodes.label: lowerbound

nodes.name: Eq. (3.23): Closed weighted tail bound
nodes.statement: \lambda^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \varepsilon^2(s,y) dy \leq 3.
nodes.label: aa3

nodes.name: Eq. (3.24): Monotonicity with j = 5/2
nodes.statement: \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}.
nodes.label: neovneogbgeo

nodes.name: Eq. (3.25): Bound on g_s
nodes.statement: \left| g_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 9 4 + 2 \beta },
nodes.label: dg

nodes.name: Eq. (3.26): Bound on lambda_s/lambda + b
nodes.statement: \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + b \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 54},
nodes.label: dl

nodes.name: Eq. (3.27): Bound on x_s/lambda - 1
nodes.statement: \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1 \right|\lesssim s^{-\frac 54}.
nodes.label: dx

nodes.name: Eq. (3.28): Lambda close to tail law
nodes.statement: & \left| \lambda (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &= \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \lambda^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber
nodes.label: bbb2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.29): ODE for x^{1/(1-beta)}
nodes.statement: \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}},
nodes.label: vnkrvrnorn

nodes.name: Eq. (3.30): Sharp asymptotics of x
nodes.statement: \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}.
nodes.label: aa2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.31): Sharp asymptotics of lambda
nodes.statement: \left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}.
nodes.label: aaa2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.32): Sharp asymptotics of b
nodes.statement: \left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}.
nodes.label: aaaa2

nodes.name: Eq. (3.33): Exit condition H(s*) = 1
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Eq. (3.34): Strict outgoing behavior
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument
nodes.label: dFdG

nodes.name: Eq. (3.35): Derivative of G at exit time
nodes.statement: G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*} +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument
nodes.label: gstar

nodes.name: Eq. (3.36): Derivative of F at exit time
nodes.statement: F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument
nodes.label: fstar

nodes.name: Eq. (3.37): Good initial parameters
nodes.statement: | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}},
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument
nodes.label: estimation

nodes.name: Eq. (A.4): Equation of q_1
nodes.statement: \partial_t q_1 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1+f_0)^5-f_0^5)=F_0,\quad q_1(0,x)= 0,
nodes.label: defquA

nodes.name: Eq. (A.5): Weight function phi_theta
nodes.statement: \varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) = x^{\bar \theta} \text{ for $x\geq 4$},\quad \varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) = e^{\frac x8} \text{ for $x\leq 0$},\quad \varphi'\geq 0,\ \varphi'''\leq \frac 14 \varphi' \text{ on $\mathbb{R}$}.
nodes.label: dfphiu

nodes.name: Eq. (A.6): Weighted bound on the source F_0
nodes.statement: \int F_0^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2} {\varphi_{\theta_1}'}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) & \lesssim \int_{x>\frac t4 + \frac {x_0} 4 + 4} x^{-2(\theta+3)} \left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 \right)^{\theta_1+1} \nonumber \\ & + \int_{\frac t8 + \frac {x_0} 8 < x<\frac t4 + \frac {x_0} 4 + 4} x^{-2(\theta+3)} +\int_{x< \frac t8 + \frac {x_0} 8} e^{\frac 18 (x-\frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 )}\nonumber \\ & \lesssim (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-4 } .
nodes.label: Fzero

nodes.name: Eq. (A.7): Weighted mass estimate
nodes.statement: M_{\theta_1}(t) + \int_0^t\int \left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2 + q_1^2 \right] \varphi_{\theta_1}' \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases}
nodes.label: eqM

nodes.name: Eq. (A.8): Weighted energy estimate
nodes.statement: & E_{\theta_1}(t) + \frac 1{10} \int_0^t \int \left[(\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 + (\partial_x q_1)^2 \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\nonumber \\ & \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases}
nodes.label: eqE

nodes.name: Eq. (A.9): Weighted L-infinity bound
nodes.statement: \|q_1^2 \sqrt{\varphi_{\theta_1+2}} \|_{L^\infty} &\lesssim \int_x^{+\infty} |q_1| |\partial_x q_1| \sqrt{\varphi_{\theta_1+2}} + \int_x^{+\infty} |q_1|^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'}{\sqrt{\varphi_{\theta_1+2}}}\nonumber\\ & \lesssim \left( \int q_1^2\right)^{\frac 12} \left( \int |\partial_x q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2} + \int |q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}\right)^{\frac 12},
nodes.label: Linfty

nodes.name: Eq. (A.10): Coercivity of E_theta1
nodes.statement: E_{\theta_1}(t) & \geq \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2} - C \int (q_1^6 + q_1^2 f_0^4) \varphi_{\theta_1+2}\nonumber\\ & \geq \frac 12 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2} - C M_{\theta_1}(t),
nodes.label: eq6

nodes.name: Eq. (A.11): Weighted H1 estimate on q_1
nodes.statement: &\int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}+ \int_0^t \int \left[(\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 + (\partial_x q_1)^2 \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\nonumber \\ &\lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases}
nodes.label: eqEbb

nodes.name: Eq. (A.12): Pointwise weighted bound on q_1
nodes.statement: q_1^2(t,x) \varphi_{\theta_1+1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) & \lesssim \int_x^{+\infty} |q_1| |\partial_x q_1| \varphi_{\theta_1+1} +\int_x^{+\infty} |q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+1}' \nonumber \\ & \lesssim \int |\partial_x q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2} +\int |q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1} ,
nodes.label: linfty

nodes.name: Eq. (A.13): Pointwise decay of q_1
nodes.statement: |q_1(t,x)| \lesssim x^{- (\frac {\theta_1}2 +\frac 12 )} t^{\frac 38} =x^{- (\theta+\frac {19}8)} t^{\frac 38} \lesssim x^{- (\theta+2)}.

nodes.statement: \nonumber & \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' \left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) dt + \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1(t))^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \\ & +|\partial_x^{k'-1} q_1(t)|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases}

nodes.label: eq:cf11

nodes.name: L2-critical generalized Korteweg--de Vries equation (gKdV)
nodes.statement: We consider the $L^2$-critical generalized Korteweg--de Vries equation (gKdV) \begin{equation} {\rm (gKdV)}\quad \left\{\begin{array}{ll} u_t + (u_{xx} + u^5)_x =0, \quad & (t,x)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}, \\ u(0,x)= u_0(x), & x\in {\mathbb R}. \end{array} \right. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Local well-posedness of gKdV in H^1 (Kenig-Ponce-Vega)
nodes.statement: The Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the energy space $H^1$ from Kenig, Ponce and Vega \cite{KPV,KPV2}. Given $u_0 \in H^1$, there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\mathop{\rm lim}_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: gKdV is locally well-posed in H^1, with a maximal solution that is global or has blowing-up derivative norm.
conclusions: there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\mathop{\rm lim}_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$

nodes.name: Conservation of mass and energy
nodes.statement: For $H^1$ solution, the mass and the energy are conserved by the flow: $\forall t\in [0,T)$, $$M(u(t))=\int u^2(t)= M(u_0), \ \ E(u(t))= \frac 12 \int u_x^2(t) - \frac 16 \int u^6(t)= E(u_0).$$
conclusions: the mass and the energy are conserved by the flow

nodes.name: Symmetries of gKdV
nodes.statement: Equation \eqref{kdv} has the following invariances: if $u(t,x)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv} then $-u(t,x)$, $ u(-t,-x)$ and $$\lambda_0^{\frac12}u(\lambda_0^3 (t-t_0),\lambda_0 (x -x_0)), \ \ (\lambda_0,t_0,x_0)\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}$$ are also solutions of \eqref{kdv}.
nodes.statement_short: Sign change, reflection and the scaling/translation group map gKdV solutions to solutions.

nodes.name: Solitons of gKdV
nodes.statement: The family of traveling wave solutions of \eqref{kdv}, called solitons, plays a distinguished role in the analysis: $$u(t,x) = Q_{\lambda_0}(x-\lambda_0^{-2} t-x_0), \ \ (\lambda_0,x_0)\in\mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R},$$ with \begin{equation} Q_\lambda(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12} }Q \left(\frac x\lambda\right) ,\quad Q(x) = \left(\frac {3}{\cosh^{2}\left( 2 x\right)}\right)^{\frac14}, \quad Q''+Q^5 =Q. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Solitons are the traveling waves Q_lambda(x - lambda^{-2}t - x_0) built from the ground state Q solving Q''+Q^5=Q.

nodes.name: Sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: \forall v\in H^1,\quad \int |v|^6 \leq \int v_x^2 \left(\frac {\int v^2}{\int Q^2}\right)^2.
nodes.label: gn

nodes.name: Global existence below the ground state mass
nodes.statement: Moreover, from \eqref{gn}, mass and energy conservations, for initial data in $H^1$ such that $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$, the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time.
assumptions: for initial data in $H^1$ such that $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$
conclusions: the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time

nodes.name: Blow up for negative energy data (Merle)
nodes.statement: In particular, from a rigidity theorem around solitons (\cite{MMjmpa}), the first proof of blow up in finite or infinite time was obtained (\cite{Mjams}) for initial data \begin{equation}\hbox {$u_0 \in H^1$ such that \eqref{utwosmall} and $E(u_0)<0$.} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.statement_short: Solutions with mass slightly above that of Q and negative energy blow up in finite or infinite time.

nodes.name: Minimal mass blow up solution
nodes.statement: \noindent{\bf Minimal mass blow up solution {\rm (\cite{MMR2}, \cite{MMduke})}.} {\it {\rm (i) Existence.} There exists a solution $S(t)\in \mathcal C((0,+\infty),H^1)$ to {\rm (\ref{kdv})} with minimal mass $\|S(t)\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$ such that \begin{equation} \| S_x(t)\|_{L^2}\sim \frac{\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{ t}\ \ \mbox{as} \ t\downarrow 0. \end{equation} \\ {\rm (ii) Uniqueness.} Let $u$ be an $H^1$ blow up solution to \eqref{kdv} with minimal mass $\|u(t)\|_{L^2} = \|Q\|_{L^2}$. Then $u=S$ up to the invariances of the (gKdV) equation.}
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.statement_short: There is a unique (up to symmetries) minimal mass blow up solution S, with blow up rate 1/t.
conclusions: There exists a solution $S(t)\in \mathcal C((0,+\infty),H^1)$ to {\rm (\ref{kdv})} with minimal mass $\|S(t)\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$
Then $u=S$ up to the invariances of the (gKdV) equation.

nodes.name: Set A of data with decay on the right and tube T
nodes.statement: More precisely, let $$ \mathcal{A}= \left\{ u_0=Q+\varepsilon_0 \hbox{ with } \|\varepsilon_0\|_{H^1}<\alpha_0 \hbox{ and } \int_{y>0} y^{10}\varepsilon_0^2< 1 \right\}, $$ $$\mathcal T_{\alpha^*}=\left\{u\in H^1\ \ \mbox{with}\ \ \inf_{\lambda_0>0, \, x_0\in \mathbb{R}} \left\|u- Q_{\lambda_0}\left( .-x_0 \right) \right\|_{L^2} <\alpha^*\right\}.$$
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.statement_short: A: H^1-small perturbations of Q with weighted decay on the right; T_{alpha*}: L^2 tube around the soliton family.

nodes.name: Classification of the flow in A
nodes.statement:
oindent{ f Classification in $\mathcal A$ {m (\cite{MMR1,MMR2})}.} Let $0<\alpha_0\ll\alpha^*\ll 1$. {\sl Let $u_0 \in \mathcal{A}$ and $u \in \mathcal C ([0,T),H^1)$ be the corresponding solution of \eqref{kdv}. Then, one of the following three scenarios occurs: \medskip 
oindent{ f (Blow up)} For all $t\in [0,T),$ $u(t)\in \mathcal{T}_{\alpha^*}$ and the solution blows up in finite time $T<+\infty$ with  egin{equation} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim  rac {\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{\ell_0 (T-t)} \quad \hbox{as $t\uparrow T$ for some $\ell_0>0$.} \end{equation}

nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.statement_short: For data in A, the solution either blows up at rate 1/(T-t), converges to a soliton, or exits the tube near the minimal mass solution S.
assumptions: Let $u_0 \in \mathcal{A}$ and $u \in \mathcal C ([0,T),H^1)$ be the corresponding solution of \eqref{kdv}.
conclusions: Then, one of the following three scenarios occurs:

Moreover, such solutions can be taken arbitrarily close in $H^1$ to the family of solitons.
nodes.label: th:1

nodes.name: Sharpness of the results of MMR1, MMR2
nodes.statement: {\it 1. Sharpness of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2}}. Theorem \ref{th:1} above shows the optimality of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2} since it proves that some decay assumption (such as $u_0\in \mathcal A$) is required to obtain a unique stable blow up rate $1/(T-t)$. This is in contrast with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, for which the stable blow up rate is obtained in $H^1$, without additional decay assumption (see \cite{MRjams} and references therein).
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 shows a decay assumption is needed for the stable 1/(T-t) rate, unlike for NLS.

nodes.name: Instability of the exotic solutions
nodes.statement: Note from the proof that the solutions obtained in Theorem \ref{th:1} are expected to be unstable (except may be for $\nu<1$ in \eqref{th:1:1}). Indeed, they are constructed using a topogical argument involving two possible directions of instability.
nodes.statement_short: The constructed exotic solutions are expected to be unstable (except possibly for nu<1).

nodes.name: Comparison with blow up for negative energy
nodes.statement: {\it 2}. It is proved in \cite{Mjams, MMannals} that initial data $u_0$ such that \eqref{classe} generate solutions that blow up in finite or infinite time. The proof is by obstruction and Liouville classification and does not provide any estimate on the blow up speed. This $H^1$ result is also sharp in the sense that from Theorem~\ref{th:1}, both finite or infinite time blow up may occur in $H^1$. All these results thus complement each other.

nodes.name: On the role of tails
nodes.statement: {\it 3. On the role of tails.} As one can see from the proof of Theorem \ref{th:1}, the blow up rate is directly related to the precise behavior of the initial data on the right. In particular, other type of blow up speeds can be produced by similar arguments by adjusting the tail of the initial data. A similar phenomenon was observed for global in time growing up solutions to the parabolic energy critical harmonic heat flow by Gustafson, Nakanishi and Tsai \cite{NT2}. There an explicit formula on the growth of the solution at infinity is given directly in terms of the initial data which is conceptually very similar to what we observe for (gKdV). Recall that continua of blow up rates were observed in pioneering works by Krieger, Schlag and Tataru \cite{KST}, \cite{KST2} for energy critical wave problems (see also Donninger and Krieger \cite{DK}). We also refer to Fila et al. \cite{FKWY} for a formal approach in the case of the energy critical heat equation. All these results point out that the sole critical topology is not enough to classify the flow near the ground state.
nodes.statement_short: The blow up rate is dictated by the tail of the data; analogous continua of rates are known for heat flow and wave problems.

nodes.name: On the decay assumption
nodes.statement: {\it 4. On the decay assumption}. In \cite{MMR1} (see the definition of $\mathcal A$), the assumption $\int y^{10} \varepsilon^2<1$ is not sharp. In Theorem \ref{th:1}, the solution contains a tail of the form $x^{-\theta}$ for $x\gg 1$, where $\theta\in(1,\frac {29}{18})$.

nodes.name: Sharp decay assumption for the stable blow up rate
nodes.statement: By now, it is not clear what is the sharp decay assumption on the initial data required to get the stable blow up rate in \cite{MMR1}.

nodes.name: Scalar product
nodes.statement: For $f,g\in L^2$, we note the scalar product: $$(f,g)=\int f(x)g(x)dx.$$

nodes.name: Generator of L2 scaling Lambda
nodes.statement: We introduce the generator of the $L^2$ scaling symmetry $$ \Lambda f=\frac12f+yf'. $$

nodes.name: Linearized operator L
nodes.statement: We let the linearized operator close to the ground state be: \begin{equation} Lf=-f''+f-5Q^4f. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Small constant delta(alpha*)
nodes.statement: For a given small constant $0<\alpha^*\ll1 $, $\delta(\alpha^*)$ denotes a small constant with $$\delta(\alpha^*)\to 0\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ \alpha^*\to 0.$$

nodes.name: Characteristic function 1_I
nodes.statement: We denote by ${\mathbf{1}}_I$ the characteristic function of the interval $I$.

nodes.name: Decomposition ansatz with tail
nodes.statement: We then consider the solution to {\rm (\ref{kdv})} with initial data $Q+f_0$ and claim that it admits a decomposition of the form \begin{equation} u(t,x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + \lambda^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,x(t)) Y_0 + \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \end{equation} for some $$\|\varepsilon(t)\|_{H^1}\ll 1$$ and where $Y_0$ is a fixed function (see Lemma \ref{lemmainvert} for the definition of $Y_0$ and Proposition \ref{le:2} for the justification of this correction term).
nodes.statement_short: The solution with data Q+f_0 decomposes as a modulated Q_b plus p Y_0 correction, small epsilon, and the tail flow q_0.

nodes.name: Formal modulation system with tail
nodes.statement: Then, explicit computations similar to the ones in \cite{MMR1} yield to leading order (neglecting $\varepsilon$ and higher order terms in $(b,\lambda,x)$) the set of coupled modulation equations in the setting of the decomposition {\rm (\ref{uu})}: \begin{equation} \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left( \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right)=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: To leading order, (b, lambda, x) obey lambda_s/lambda+b=0, x_s=lambda and conservation of b/lambda^2 plus a tail term.

nodes.name: Unperturbed modulation system and universal blow up regime
nodes.statement: This system is to be compared to the unperturbed one obtained in \cite{MMR1}, for $u_0\in \mathcal{A}$ (without tail): \begin{equation} \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}, \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2}\right) =0,\end{equation} which leads to the universal blow up regime $$\frac b{\lambda^2} = \ell_0, \ \ \lambda(t) = \ell_0 (T-t)\ \ \mbox{for some}\ \ \ell_0>0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Without tail, conservation of b/lambda^2 yields the universal regime lambda(t) = l_0 (T-t).

nodes.name: Formal integration of the perturbed modulation system
nodes.statement: We now integrate explicitly {\rm (\ref{dynsyst})} and fit the parameters of the tail $(c_0,\theta)$ to obtain the blow up regimes described in Theorem \ref{th:1}. Integrating in $s$, we find $$ \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} =\ell_0, $$ where $\ell_0$ is a constant. We focus on the threshold regime $\ell_0=0$ leading to: \begin{equation} \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}=0, \end{equation} which can now be integrated as follows: $$ \lambda^{-\frac 12}\lambda_s = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda x^{-\theta} = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 x_s x^{-\theta} $$ or equivalently after integration: $$ \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s) = \ell_1. $$ We focus again on the threshold regime $\ell_1=0$ leading to: $$ \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) = -\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s). $$ We see that $c_0<0$ is necessary at this point and $$ x_s(s) = \lambda(s) = \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 x^{-2 \theta+2}(s). $$ By integration on $[s_0,s]$, choosing $ x^{2\theta-1}(s_0)=(2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s_0$, we obtain $$ x^{2\theta-1}(s) = (2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s, $$ and thus $$ \lambda(s) = (2\theta- 1)^{\frac {-2\theta+2}{2\theta-1}} \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1} c_0\right)^{\frac {2}{2 \theta-1}} s^{- \frac {2(\theta-1)}{2\theta-1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the formal system twice, selecting the threshold constants l_0 = l_1 = 0, then integrate x_s = lambda explicitly.

nodes.name: Explicit threshold solution of the formal system
nodes.statement: Set $$ \beta = \frac { 2(\theta-1)} {2\theta-1},\quad \theta = \frac {1-\frac \beta2}{1-\beta}, \quad c_0 =-\frac { \int Q}2(\theta-1) (2\theta-1)^{\theta-1} ,$$ so that \begin{equation} \lambda(s) = s^{-\beta}, \quad x(s) = \frac 1{1-\beta} s^{1-\beta},\quad b(s) =\frac {\beta}s. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: With beta, theta, c_0 so related, lambda = s^{-beta}, x = s^{1-beta}/(1-beta), b = beta/s solve the formal system.

nodes.name: Two instability directions
nodes.statement: Of course, one can check directly that \eqref{eq:blx} are solutions of the system \eqref{dynsyst} but the above computation reveals the two instability directions \begin{equation} \ell_0=\ell_1= 0, \end{equation} and justifies the use of a topological argument to construct the solution.

nodes.name: Heuristic control of the remainder
nodes.statement: We now aim at constructing an exact solution which corresponds to control the remainder term $\varepsilon(t,x)$. Note that we may now choose $\varepsilon_0(x)$ to be {\it well localized on the right}, and we therefore adapt the machinery developed in \cite{MMR1} to construct a mixed energy/Virial functional $$\mathcal F\sim \int\psi\varepsilon_y^2+\varphi\varepsilon^2-\frac 13 \psi\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon\right]$$ for well chosen cut off functions $(\psi,\varphi)$ which are exponentially decaying to the left, and polynomially growing to the right. Roughly speaking, in the above regime \eqref{eq:blx}, this functional enjoys two fundamental properties: \\ -- Coercivity : $$\mathcal F \gtrsim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2.$$ -- Lyapounov monotonicity : \begin{equation} \frac{d}{ds}\left\{s^j {\mathcal F}\right\}+ s^j \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2 \lesssim s^{j-4}, \ \ j\geq 0. \end{equation} Time integration of the monotonicity formula {\rm (\ref{cnkneneoe})} in the regime dictated by {\rm (\ref{eq:blx})} yields sufficient uniform estimates on $\varepsilon$. Therefore, it only remains to adjust the initial parameters $(b(s_0),\lambda(s_0))$ in order to asymptotically satisfy the unstable conditions {\rm (\ref{unstabomodesintro})}. This is achieved using a simple topological argument, as in \cite{MMC} but in a blow up setting (see also \cite{RH}, \cite{S}, \cite{MRR}, \cite{CoteZaag}).
nodes.statement_short: A mixed energy/virial functional, coercive and monotone, controls epsilon; a topological argument handles the unstable directions.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 from the parameter asymptotics (step iv)
nodes.statement:
oindent (iv) \emph{Conclusion of the proof returning to the original time variable.} The above strategy is implemented for all $0< eta< rac{11}{20}$. Now we show how the behavior of the parameters {m (ef{eq:blx})} (see the precise estimates in \eqref{sharp}) in renormalized time leads to the scenarios of Theorem ef{th:1} in the original time $t$ (after possible scaling and time translation to adjust constants). \smallskip 
oindent{-- Blow up in finite time:} for $  rac 13 <  eta <  rac {11}{20}. $ From \eqref{sharpintro}, {m (ef{eq:blx})}: $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\lambda^3(s)} ds=T<+\infty$$ and the solution $u(t)$ blows up in finite time $T$. Moreover, $$ T-t=\int_{s(t)}^{+\infty}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} \sim  rac {s^{ -( 3  eta-1)}}{3 eta-1} , \quad \lambda(t) \sim \left[ (3 eta-1)(T-t)ight]^{ rac { eta}{3 eta-1}}, $$ which implies $\|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \|Q'\|_{L^2} \lambda^{-1} (t) \sim C (T-t)^{-
u}$ for any $
u\in ( rac {11}{13},+\infty).$ \medskip 
oindent{-- Grow up in infinite time:} for $  eta =  rac 13, $ the solution $u(t)$ is global in time since $\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\lambda^3(s)} ds =+\infty$. Moreover, for some $c_0$ and some $c_1 >0$, $$ t=\int_{s_0}^{s(t)}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} = {m log} s + c_0 +O(s^{- rac 1{10}}),\quad s\sim c_1 e^t ,\quad \lambda(t)\sim c_1^{- rac 13} e^{- rac t 3} . $$ This means grow up in infinite time for $u(t)$ with exponential growth. Scaling and time translation lead to any exponential rate $e^{-ct}$, $c>0$. Finally, for $0< eta<  rac 13,$ we also obtain a global solution $u(t)$ since $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \lambda^3(s) ds \geq 2^{-3} \int_{s_0}^{+\infty} s^{-3  eta} ds = +\infty,$$ and $$t= \int_{s_0}^{t(s)} \lambda^3(s') ds' \sim  rac 1{1-3  eta} s^{1-3  eta} , \quad \lambda(t) \sim (1-3  eta)^{ rac  eta{1-3  eta}} t^{ rac  eta{1-3  eta}} , $$ which means grow up rates $t^
u$ at $+\infty$, for any $
u= rac { eta}{1-3 eta}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables back to t via ds/dt = lambda^{-3}, split by beta: beta>1/3 gives finite time blow up, beta=1/3 exponential and beta<1/3 power grow up.

nodes.name: Function space Y
nodes.statement: Let the functional space ${\mathcal Y}$ be the set of functions $f\in \mathcal C^\infty({{\mathbb R}},{{\mathbb R}})$ such that \begin{equation} \forall k\in \mathbb{N},\ \exists C_k,\, r_k>0,\ \forall y\in {{\mathbb R}},\quad |f^{(k)}(y)|\leq C_k (1+|y|)^{r_k} {e^{-|y|}}, \end{equation} and $L$ be the linearized operator close to $Q$ given by {\rm (\ref{deflplus})}.
nodes.genus: the set of functions $f\in \mathcal C^\infty({{\mathbb R}},{{\mathbb R}})$

nodes.name: Invertibility of L (Lemma 2.1)
nodes.statement: {\rm (i)} There exists a unique $Y_0\in \mathcal Y$, even, such that \begin{equation} L Y_0= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,Y_0)=-\frac 34 \int Q . \end{equation} {\rm (ii)} There exists a unique function $P$ such that $P' \in \mathcal{Y}$ and \begin{equation} (L P)'={\Lambda} Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to -\infty} P(y) = \frac 12 \int Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to +\infty} P(y) =0, \end{equation} \begin{equation} (P, Q) = \frac 1{16} \left(\int Q\right)^2 > 0,\quad (P, Q')=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: There is a unique even Y_0 in Y with L Y_0 = 5Q^4 and a unique P with (LP)' = Lambda Q, prescribed limits and (P,Q)>0.
conclusions: There exists a unique $Y_0\in \mathcal Y$, even, such that
There exists a unique function $P$ such that $P' \in \mathcal{Y}$ and
nodes.label: lemmainvert

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Note that the existence and uniqueness of $Y_0$ follows readily from standard properties of the operator $L$ (see e.g. \cite{MMR1}). Moreover, $$ (Q,Y_0)= -\frac 12 (L\Lambda Q,Y_0) =-\frac 12(\Lambda Q,5Q^4 ) =-\frac 34 \int Q^5=-\frac 34 \int Q. $$ Part (ii) is taken from \cite{MMR1}, Proposition 2.2.
nodes.statement_short: Existence from standard properties of L; compute (Q,Y_0) via L Lambda Q = -2Q; part (ii) quoted from MMR1.

nodes.name: Cut-off chi_b
nodes.statement: More precisely, let $\chi\in {\mathcal C}^{\infty}({\mathbb R})$ be such that $0\leq \chi \leq 1$, $\chi'\geq 0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, $\chi\equiv 1$ on $[-1,+\infty)$, $\chi\equiv 0$ on $(-\infty,-2]$, and define \begin{equation} \chi_b(y)= \chi\left(|b|^{\gamma} {y} \right),\ \ \gamma = \frac 34. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Approximate self-similar profiles Q_b (Lemma 2.2)
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y). \end{equation} Then:\\ {\rm (i) Estimates on $Q_b$:} For all $y \in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |Q_b(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| \left( {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,0]}(|b|^\gamma y) + e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \\ & |Q_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} +|b|^{1+k \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,-1]}(|b|^\gamma y),\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} \noindent {\rm (ii) Equation of $Q_b$:} let \begin{equation} -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b, \end{equation} then, for all $y\in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |\Psi_b(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 \left(e^{-\frac {|y|} 2}+ {\mathbf{1}}_{[- 2,0]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) \right), \\ & |\Psi_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ (k+1) \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 e^{-\frac {|y|} 2} ,\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} {\rm (iii) Mass and energy properties of $Q_b$:} \begin{align} & \left|\int Q_b^2 - \left( \int Q^2 + 2b \int PQ \right)\right| \lesssim |b|^{2-\gamma}, \\ & \left| E(Q_b) + b \int PQ\right|\lesssim b^2 . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The profiles Q_b = Q + b chi_b P satisfy pointwise bounds, solve the self-similar equation up to Psi_b = O(b^2), and have mass/energy expansions in b.
nodes.label: cl:2

nodes.name: Slowly decaying tail f_0
nodes.statement: Let $c_0<0$, $x_0\gg 1$, $\theta>1$ and let $f_0$ be a smooth function such that \begin{equation} f_0(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}c_0 x^{-\theta} & \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\\ 0 & \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$,}\end{array}\right. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim |x|^{-\theta - k}, \ \ \forall (x,k)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{N}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right

nodes.name: Tail solution q_0
nodes.statement: Let $q_0$ be the solution of \begin{equation} \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad q_0(0,x)= f_0(x). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of q_0 (Lemma 2.3)
nodes.statement: The solution $q_0$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded in $H^1$. Moreover, $\forall t\geq 0,\ \forall x>\frac t 2+\frac {x_0}2$, \begin{equation} \forall k\geq 0,\quad |\partial_x^k q_0(t,x) -f_0^{(k)}(x) | \lesssim t^{\frac 38} x^{-\theta-\frac {19}8 - k } \lesssim x^{-\theta-2 - k }, \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\partial_tq_0(t,x) | \lesssim x^{-\theta-3} . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.statement_short: The gKdV flow of the tail is global, bounded in H^1 and keeps the x^{-theta} decay of f_0 for x > t/2 + x_0/2.
conclusions: The solution $q_0$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded in $H^1$.
nodes.label: le:qz

nodes.name: w = u - q_0
nodes.statement: Consider $u(t,x)$ a solution of \eqref{kdv} and set \begin{equation} w(t,x)= u(t,x) - q_0(t,x). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Closeness of w to the soliton
nodes.statement: We assume that $w$ is close to $Q$ in the following sense : there exist $(\lambda_1(t),x_1(t))\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}$ and $\varepsilon_1(t)$ such that \begin{align} \forall t\in [0,t_0], \ \ & \lambda_1(t)<\frac {10}9 \lambda_0,\quad x_1(t)> \frac 9{10} x_0, \\ & w(t,x)=\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}_1(t)}(Q+\varepsilon_1)\left(t,\frac{x-x_1(t)}{\lambda_1(t)}\right) \end{align} with \begin{equation} \forall t\in [0,t_0],\ \ \|\varepsilon_1(t)\|_{L^2}+\left(\int (\partial_y \varepsilon_1)^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} dy \right)^{\frac 12}\leq \alpha^* \end{equation} for some small enough universal constant $\alpha^*>0$.

nodes.name: Preliminary estimates and modulation equations (Proposition 2.4)
nodes.statement_short: Modulated decomposition with orthogonality conditions, conservation-law bounds on epsilon, and modulation equations for (b, lambda, x) including the tail term.
assumptions: Assume {\rm (\ref{decompo0})}--{\rm (\ref{hypeprochien})} for $\alpha^*$ small enough, and assume $x_0$ large enough and $\lambda_0$ small enough.
nodes.label: le:2

nodes.name: Remark 2.5: justification of the formal system
nodes.statement: The bounds \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond} will justify the dynamical system {\rm (\ref{dynsyst})}.
