nodes.statement_short: Direct estimates from the tail asymptotics of Lemma 2.3, splitting space into near and far regions; parity for projections.

nodes.name: Parameters beta, theta and c_0
nodes.statement: Let $$ \beta = \frac { 2(\theta-1)} {2\theta-1},\quad \theta = \frac {1-\frac \beta2}{1-\beta}, \quad 0< \beta< \frac {11}{20}, \quad 1<\theta <\frac {29}{18},$$ and define \begin{equation} c_0=-\frac {\int Q}2(\theta-1)(2\theta-1)^{\theta-1}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Functions g and f
nodes.statement: Given $s>s_0$, $(b(s),\lambda(s),x(s))\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}$, we define: $$ g(s) =\frac {b(s)}{\lambda^2(s)} + \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s),\quad f(s) = \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}. $$

nodes.name: Weight functions phi_i and psi
nodes.statement: Let $(\varphi_i)_{i=1,2},\psi$ be smooth functions such that: \begin{eqnarray} \varphi_i(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{lll}e^{y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1+y \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ -\frac 12<y<\frac 12,\\ y^i\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>2, \end{array}\right. \ \ \varphi_i'(y) >0, \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \end{eqnarray} \begin{eqnarray} \psi(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} e^{2y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1 \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>-\tfrac 12,\end{array}\right. \ \ \psi'(y) \geq 0 \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Norms N_i and N_{i,loc}
nodes.statement: Let $B> 100$ and $$\psi_B(y)=\psi\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ \varphi_{i,B}=\varphi_i\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ i=1,2,$$ and define the following norms on $\varepsilon$ \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_i} (s) = \int \varepsilon_y^2(s,y) \psi_{B}(y)dy + \int \varepsilon^2(s,y) \varphi_{i,B}(y) dy, \end{equation} \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}} (s) = \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi'_{i,B} (y) dy,\quad i=1,2. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bootstrap (Proposition 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let $s_0=s_0(\beta)>1$ large enough and set \begin{equation} x_0= x (s_0)= \frac 1{(1-\beta)}{s_0^{1-\beta}}. \end{equation} Let $\varepsilon_0\in H^1$ be such that \begin{equation} s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \varepsilon^2_0(y) dy+\|\varepsilon_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\varepsilon_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\varepsilon_0,\Lambda Q) =(\varepsilon_0,Q)=0.\end{equation} Then, there exists \begin{equation} (\lambda_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\lambda,b) \ : \ | \lambda - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\}, \end{equation} such that the solution of \eqref{kdv} with initial data \begin{equation} u_0(x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \lambda^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) Y_0+ \varepsilon_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\lambda_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x) \end{equation} has a decomposition $(b(s),\lambda(s),x(s), \varepsilon(s))$ as in Proposition \ref{le:2} which satisfies\footnote{recall that $s=s(t)$ is the rescaled time {\rm (\ref{rescaledtime})}.} on $[s_0,+\infty)$: $$\leqno{\rm (BS1)}\quad \left(|g(s)| s^{1 - 2 \beta + \frac 15} \right)^2+ \left(|f(s)| s^{\frac \beta 2 + \frac 1{10}}\right)^2\leq 1; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS2)}\quad |b(s)|\leq {10} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 10 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 10 s^{1-\beta}; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS3)}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,y)dy\leq 10 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$ Moreover, \begin{equation} \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \lambda^{-1} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}+ \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For suitable initial parameters (lambda_0,b_0) in D, the solution satisfies the bootstrap bounds for all s and lambda ~ s^{-beta}, x ~ s^{1-beta}/(1-beta), b ~ beta/s.
nodes.label: PR:BS

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 from Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Let us observe that {\rm (\ref{sharp})} now gives the leading order behavior of the scaling parameter $\lambda(s)=\frac{1}{s^{\beta}}(1+o(1))$, and the conclusion of Theorem \ref{th:1} now immediately follow from the change of variables {\rm (\ref{rescaledtime})} depending on the value of $\beta$ as in step (iv) of section \ref{vneovnoen}.
nodes.statement_short: The sharp asymptotics lambda(s) ~ s^{-beta} plus the change of variables ds/dt = lambda^{-3} give the three regimes.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (setup by contradiction)
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS}. First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that $$ b_0=b(s_0),\quad \lambda(s_0)=\lambda_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \varepsilon(s_0)=\varepsilon_0. $$ We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$, we have $$ s^*(\lambda_0,b_0) := \mathop{\rm sup} \left\{ s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$} \right\} <+\infty. $$ We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\lambda_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: assume every (lambda_0,b_0) in D has a finite exit time s*, close the bootstrap and conclude by topology.

nodes.name: Claim 2: consequences of the bootstrap estimates
nodes.statement: {\rm (i)} For $s_0=s_0(\beta)$ large enough, there holds: \begin{itemize} \item if $\beta>\frac 13$, for all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, $t(s)= \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds'<1$; \item if $0<\beta\leq \frac 13$, for all $t>0$, $x(t) \geq \frac 23 t + \frac 23 {x_0}$. \end{itemize} {\rm (ii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \begin{equation} 0< -p(s) \lesssim \frac 1 s,\quad \frac {\lambda}{x} \lesssim \frac 1 s, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right| + \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \right| \lesssim \frac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12},\quad \left| x_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\beta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} \right) , \end{equation} \begin{equation} |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac 1{s^2}, \end{equation} \begin{align} & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2} +\frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right) \right| \nonumber \\ &\lesssim \frac 1{\lambda^2} \left( \frac 1{s^{\frac {29}{10}}} + \frac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}\right). \end{align} {\rm (iii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \begin{align} &\|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2\right|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\\ & \frac 1{\lambda^2} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{- \frac 1{10}} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} . \end{align}
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.statement_short: Under the bootstrap bounds, t(s) stays bounded or x(t) stays ahead of 2t/3, and the modulation equations give explicit decay rates.
nodes.label: le:3.1

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2
nodes.statement: Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right) <1 $$ for $s_0$ large enough. For $\beta = \frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, {\rm log}\frac s{s_0} \quad \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}. $$ Thus, $$ x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 . $$ for $s_0$ large enough. Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^3 + \frac 12 x_0$. Finally, for $0<\beta <\frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right) $$ so that for $s_0$ large $$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}}, $$ and $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15 t^{1+\beta}.$$ Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.\\ The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that $$ 0< p \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s. $$ The estimates \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are immediate consequences of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on beta (above, at, below 1/3) integrating lambda^3, then plug bootstrap bounds into the modulation equations.

nodes.name: Improved bootstrap bound (BS3')
nodes.statement: We now close the bounds on $\varepsilon$ and claim the improved bound: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$, $$\leqno{\rm (BS3')}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,x)dx\leq 5 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq \frac 12 s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$
nodes.statement_short: The weighted tail and N_i bounds on epsilon improve by a factor 2 on [s_0,s*].

nodes.name: Weight phi_10
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi_{10}$ be a smooth function such that $$\varphi_{10}(y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\leq 0, \\ y^{10}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\geq 1\end{array}\right., \quad 0\leq \varphi_{10}\lesssim \varphi_{10}' \hbox{ for $0<y<1$}.$$

nodes.name: Dynamical control of the tail on the right (Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: For all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,\begin{equation} {\lambda^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\lambda^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The y^{10}-weighted L^2 norm of epsilon grows at most like the local norm plus s^{-2}.
nodes.label: lemmatail

nodes.name: Monotonicity formula (Lemma 3.3)
nodes.statement: There exist $\mu>0$ such that the following holds for $B>100$ large enough. Let the energy--virial Lyapounov functionals for $i=1,2$, \begin{align} {\mathcal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \\ &- \frac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\right)\right)\psi_B\Big] .\nonumber \end{align} Then the following estimates hold on $[s_0, s^*]$:\\ {\em (i) Lyapounov control}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$ \begin{equation} \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} . \end{equation} {\em (iii) Coercivity of $\mathcal F_{i}$ and pointwise bounds}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$, \begin{equation} -\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The energy-virial functionals F_i satisfy a Lyapunov-type monotonicity inequality and are coercive in N_i up to s^{-4}.
nodes.label: propasymtp

nodes.name: Proof of (BS3')
nodes.statement: \noindent \textbf{Proof of {\rm (BS3')}.} From Lemma \ref{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), $$ \frac d{ds} \left\{ \lambda^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2 \right\} \lesssim \lambda^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} + s^{-2}\right) \lesssim s^{-10 \beta -2}, $$ so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2}, $$ \lambda^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s) \leq \lambda^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10\beta} \leq 2. $$ By the properties of $\varphi_{10}$ and \eqref{A2}, we obtain \begin{equation} \lambda^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \varepsilon^2(s,y) dy \leq 3. \end{equation} Now, we apply Lemma \ref{propasymtp} with $j=\frac 52 $. We find by \eqref{lyapounovconrolbis} and $\beta< \frac {11}{20}$, \begin{equation} \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}. \end{equation} The initial smallness {\rm (\ref{A2})} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of {\rm (\ref{neovneogbgeo})} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields: $$ \mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} $$ for some $\delta=\delta(\beta)>0$. Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude: $$ \mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq \frac 12 s^{- \frac 52} $$ for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws {\rm (\ref{twobound})}, {\rm (\ref{energbound})} concludes the proof of (BS3').
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the tail monotonicity of Lemma 3.2 and the Lyapunov control of Lemma 3.3 with j=5/2, then use coercivity.

nodes.name: Improved bootstrap bound (BS2')
nodes.statement: We claim: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,$$\leqno{\rm (BS2')}\quad |b(s)|\leq {5} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 5 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 5 s^{1-\beta}. $$
nodes.statement_short: b, lambda and x stay within a factor 5 of beta/s, s^{-beta} and s^{1-beta}/(1-beta).

nodes.name: Proof of (BS2')
nodes.statement: \textbf{Proof of (BS2').} First, note that from \eqref{fond}, \eqref{eq:2002bis}, and using (BS2)-(BS3), $\frac 13 \leq \beta\leq \frac 9{10}$, we have on $[s_0,s^*]$: \begin{equation} \left| g_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 9 4 + 2 \beta }, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + b \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 54}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1 \right|\lesssim s^{-\frac 54}. \end{equation} By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1-\beta)(\theta-1) =\frac \beta 2$ the estimate: \begin{align} & \left| \lambda (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &= \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \lambda^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber \end{align} Using \eqref{dx}, we find $$ \left| x_s (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}} + s^{-\frac 54 - \beta } \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}. $$ and hence\begin{equation} \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} from $2\theta-1=\frac 1{1-\beta}$ and the choice of $c_0$ in {\rm (\ref{defcobeta})} which gives: $$ (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)}= (2\theta-1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2. $$ Since from {\rm (\ref{initixzero})}: $$ \frac {(1-\beta) }{s_0^{1-\beta}} x (s_0)= 1,$$ the time integration of {\rm (\ref{vnkrvrnorn})} on $[s_0,s]$ yields $$ \left|x^{\frac 1{\beta-1}}(s) - (1-\beta)^{-\frac 1{\beta-1}} s \right| \lesssim s^{1-\frac 1{10}}. $$ Thus, \begin{equation} \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} Inserting \eqref{aa2} into \eqref{bbb2}, we find for $\lambda$, \begin{equation} \left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} Finally, using $|g(s)| \leq s^{-1 + 2 \beta - \frac 1{5}}$, we find \begin{equation} \left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} From \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2}, (BS2') follows for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Use the bootstrap bound on f to relate lambda to x, integrate the resulting ODE for x, then deduce lambda and b.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (topological argument)
nodes.statement: We now claim from a standard topological argument based on the ougoing behavior of the ODE's for $(f,g)$ that we can find $(b_0,\lambda_0)\in \mathcal D$ such that the remaining condition $(BS1)$ is closed.\\ Indeed, let $$ G(s) = g(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},\quad F(s) = f(s) s^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}, $$ and $$ H(s) = F^2(s) + G^2(s). $$ From (BS2') and (BS3'), since $s^*=s^*(x_0,b_0)<+\infty$, it follows from a standard continuity argument that at $s=s^* \geq s_0,$ \begin{equation} H(s^*)=1. \end{equation} We first claim the strict outgoing behavior: \begin{equation} H'(s^*)\geq \frac {1}{20 s^*}. \end{equation} \emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.} Since $$ G'(s) = \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) g(s)s^{-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}} +g'(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}}, $$ we have using {\rm (\ref{dFdG})}: \begin{equation} G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*} +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right). \end{equation} Similarly, $$ F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1} + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}. $$ We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx} and (BS1)-(BS2), \begin{align*} f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 x_s x^{-\theta} \\ & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[ \frac b{\lambda^2} - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right] +O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\ &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) = O\left(s^{-1 -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right). \end{align*} Thus, \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). \end{equation} Therefore $$ H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right) \geq \frac 1{20s^*}, $$ for $s_0$ large enough. \medskip By standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}), the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$ is continuous. We define the continuous maps \begin{align*} \lambda_0(F_0) &= s_0^{-\beta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}} \right)^2 \\ b_0(F_0,G_0) &= \beta s_0^{-1+\frac \beta 2} \lambda_0^{\frac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{\frac 32\beta - \frac 1{5}} \lambda_0^{\frac 32} (F_0) \right)\\ & = \beta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right| \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{- \frac 1{5}} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|^3 \right) \end{align*} so that \begin{align*} G_0 &= s_0^{1-2 \beta +\frac 1{5}} \left( \frac {b_0}{\lambda_0^2} - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda_0^{-\frac 32} x_0^{-\theta}\right)\\ F_0 &= s_0^{\frac \beta 2 +\frac 1{10}} \left( \lambda_0^{\frac 12} +\frac 2{\int Q} c_0 \frac 1{\theta-1} x_0^{-\theta+1} \right). \end{align*} Now, consider the continous map \begin{align*} \mathcal M \ : \ \ \ \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2} &\to \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\ (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right). \end{align*} where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have $\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, $\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map $\mathcal M$ is in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem. Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that \begin{equation} | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\ Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\ This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument
nodes.statement_short: Brouwer-type topological argument: strict outgoing behavior at the exit time makes the exit map a retraction of the disc onto the circle. Key step: H'(s*) >= 1/(20 s*).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement_short: Weighted monotonicity (mass, energy, higher derivative) estimates for q_1 = q_0 - f_0 with weights moving at speed 1/4. Higher derivatives by induction on k.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: We compute from {\rm (\ref{eqofeps})}: \begin{align*} &\frac 12\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2 = \int \varepsilon_s \varepsilon \varphi_{10}\\ &=\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\bigg[\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\Lambda \varepsilon+\left(-\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon - (\varepsilon +pY_0 +Q_b )^5 + Q_b ^5 +p5 Q^4 Y_0\right)_y \\ & - p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4(p-q))_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0+\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b + \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon +pY_0)_y \\ & + \Phi_{{b}} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y\bigg]. \end{align*} We integrate by parts the linear term and use $y\varphi_{10}'={10}\varphi_{10}$ for $y\geq 1$ and $\varphi_{10}'''\ll \varphi_{10}'$ for $y$ large enough to derive the bound \begin{eqnarray*} &&\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\left[\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\Lambda \varepsilon+\left(-\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right)_y\right] \\& = & -\frac12\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int y\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2-\frac 32\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon_y^2-\frac12\int\varphi'_{10}\varepsilon^2+\frac 12\int\varphi_{10}'''\varepsilon^2\\ & \leq & -\frac{10}2\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int \varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2-\frac 14\int\varphi_{10}'(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)+C\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}. \end{eqnarray*} By integration by parts in the nonlinear term, we can remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$ to obtain (using $|Q_b|+|(Q_b)_y|\leq Ce^{-\frac 12 {y}}$ for $y>0$) \begin{eqnarray*} \left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon \left[(\varepsilon +Q_b )^5 -Q_b ^5\right]_y\right| &\lesssim & \int_{y>0} \varphi_{10}e^{-\frac 12 {y}}\varepsilon^2(|\varepsilon|^3 +1) +\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^6\\ & \lesssim & \int_{y>0} e^{-\frac 14 {y}} \varepsilon^2(|\varepsilon|^3 +1)+\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^6\end{eqnarray*} Thus, by standard Sobolev estimates, \begin{eqnarray*} \left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon \left[(\varepsilon +Q_b )^5 -Q_b ^5\right]_y\right| \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\delta(\alpha^*)\int\varphi'_{10}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2). \end{eqnarray*} Next, by the bootstrap estimates, \begin{align*} & \left| \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon \left[ (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0)^5 - 5 p Q^4 Y_0 - (\varepsilon+Q_b)^5\right]_y\right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y>10} \varepsilon e^{-\frac 12 y}\left(p^2 + |b||p| + |p| (|\varepsilon|+|\varepsilon|^5 \right) \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. \end{align*} By \eqref{BSbsps} and $Y_0 \in \mathcal{Y}$, $$ \left| p_s \int Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right| \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. $$ By \eqref{cl.2} and \eqref{BSp}, \begin{align*} & \left| \int 5 (Q^4 (p-q))_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10}\right| =\left| \int 5 (p-q) e^{-4 |y|} (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y \right| \\ &\leq C \frac 1{s^2} \int (|\varepsilon_y|+|\varepsilon|) e^{-|y|}\varphi_{10} \leq \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{10} + C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^2}. \end{align*} By \eqref{BSparam}, $$ \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \int \Lambda Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right| \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. $$ The terms involving the geometrical parameters are controlled from the exponential localization of $Q_b$ on the right and {\rm (\ref{BSlsl})}--{\rm (\ref{BSparam})}: $$\left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(\Lambda Q_b)\right|\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$ \begin{align*}\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\right|&\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\left[\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}+\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2\right]\\ &\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}+\delta(\alpha^*) \int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2,\end{align*} $$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Phi_b\right|\lesssim |b_s| \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$ We control similarily the interaction with the error from {\rm (\ref{eq:202})}: $$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Psi_b\right|\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$ Finally, we claim \begin{equation} \left| \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon W_y\right| \leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2} + \frac 1{50} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}' \end{equation} We only treat the first term in $W$, the other terms are similar and easier. First, integrating by parts, we remove the derivative from $\varepsilon$ to obtain derivative on $q$, $\varphi_{10}$. Indeed, \begin{align*} & - \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} = \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right] (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y\\ & =\int \bigg\{\left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5- (Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]_y \\ &- 5(Q_b+pY_0)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] + 20 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \bigg\}q\varphi_{10} \\ &+ 5\int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q\varphi_{10}' \\ & = - \int \left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5-(Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right] (q_y\varphi_{10}+q \varphi_{10}') \\ &- 5\int \left\{(Q_b+pY_0)_y \left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] - 4 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \right\} q\varphi_{10} \\ & + 5 \int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q \varphi_{10}' . \end{align*} From the above expression, we obtain for $s$ large enough (using $\|\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1}\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*)$ and $\|q\|_{L^\infty(y>0)} \lesssim \frac 1s$) \begin{align*} &\left| \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} \right|\\ & \lesssim \int (|q|+|q_y|) e^{-\frac {|y|}2} (|\varepsilon|+|p|+|b|)|\varepsilon| +\int (|q_y|\varphi_{10} + |q|\varphi_{10}') |\varepsilon|^5 \\ & \leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2} + \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'+\delta(\alpha^*)\int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} . \end{align*} To control the last term above, we use $q_y(t,y)=\lambda^{\frac 32} \partial_x q_0(t,\lambda y + x(t)) $ so that $ |q_y(t,y)|\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 32} (\lambda y +x(t))^{-\theta-1} \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}(t) (y+1)^{-1}, $ for $y>10$, and $$ \int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} \lesssim \frac {\lambda^{\frac 12}}{x^{\theta}} \int_{y>0} \varepsilon^2 (y+1)^{-1} \varphi_{10} \leq \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'. $$ The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2+{10}\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$ and {\rm (\ref{keyestimate})} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Energy identity for the y^{10}-weighted L^2 norm, with each term of the epsilon equation bounded by the local norm and s^{-2}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: {\bf step 1} Weighted $L^2$ controls at the right. We first recall from \cite{MMR1}, proof of Proposition 3.1, the following controls for all $s\in [0,s_0]$, \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}y\varepsilon^2(s)\lesssim \left(1+\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac{10}9}(s)}\right)\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}(s), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}y^2\varepsilon^2(s)\lesssim \left(1+\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac {10}9}(s)}\right)\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}(s), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}|\varepsilon(s)|\lesssim \mathcal N_2^{\frac{1}{2}}(s). \end{equation} \medskip {\bf step 2} Algebraic computations on $\mathcal F_{i}$. First, note that the equation of $\varepsilon$ \eqref{eqofeps} can be rewritten as follows: \begin{align} \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon -\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon - Z\right)_y \\ & -p_s Y_0 +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p Y_0)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} , \end{align} where $$ Z=(Q_b+pY_0+q+ \varepsilon )^5 -Q_b^5 - 5Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5, $$ $$\Phi_b = - {b}_{s} \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P,\quad -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b.$$ We compute \begin{align*} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] &= 2\int \psi_B(\varepsilon_y)_s \varepsilon_y\\ & + 2\int \varepsilon_s \left[ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right]\\ & -2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_s \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \\& + 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon + \frac j s \mathcal F_{i} \end{align*} which we rewrite \begin{equation} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] = f^{(i)}_{1}+f^{(i)}_2+f^{(i)}_3, \end{equation} where {\allowdisplaybreaks \begin{align*} f^{(i)}_{1} &= 2 \int \left( \varepsilon_{s} - {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} {\Lambda} \varepsilon\right) \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ\right) ,\\ f^{(i,j)}_2 &= 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_B Z \right) +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}, \\ f^{(i)}_3 &= - 2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\ &+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon. \end{align*} } We claim the following estimates on the above terms: for some $\mu_0>0$, \begin{align} & \frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{1}\leq - \mu_0 \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}, \\ & \left|\frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{k}\right|\leq \frac {\mu_0}{10} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}+ C s^{10\beta -9}, \quad \hbox{for $k=2,3.$} \end{align} Inserting \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2} into {\rm (\ref{eqfnoneoge})} yields {\rm (\ref{lyapounovconrolbis})} for all $j$. In steps 3 - step 5, we prove \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2}. Observe that the definitions of $\varphi_i$ and $\psi$ imply the following estimates: \begin{align} \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad &|\varphi_i'''(y) | + | \varphi_i''(y) |+|\psi'''(y)|+|y\psi'(y)|+|\psi(y)| \lesssim \varphi'_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i(y),\\ \forall y\in (-\infty,2], \quad & e^{ |y|} \psi(y) + e^{ |y|} \psi'(y) +\varphi_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i'(y),\\ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad & \varphi_2'(y)\lesssim \varphi_1(y) \lesssim \varphi'_2(y). \end{align} In particular, \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim{\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{1}} (s)\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_2} (s),\quad \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi_{1,B} (y) dy\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) . \end{equation} {\bf step 3} Control of $f_1^{(i)}$. Proof of \eqref{re1}. We compute $ f_{1}^{(i)} $ using \eqref{eqebis} \begin{align*} \rm f_{1}^{(i)}& = 2 \int \left( -\varepsilon_{yy} {+} \varepsilon {-}Z \right)_y \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y{+}\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}{-}\psi_BZ \right) \\ & +2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q_b \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z \right) \\ & + 2 \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) \int (Q_b + \varepsilon+pY_0)_y \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Phi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Psi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + \int \left(-p_sY_0 +(5Q^4(p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0\right) \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & = {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,1}}+ {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,2}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,3}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,4}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,5}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,6}}. \end{align*} \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}: We first integrate by parts \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right] \psi_B \\ & + & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). \end{eqnarray*} We compute the various terms : \begin{align*} & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2\\ & =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2 - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\ & -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}. \end{align*} Next after integration by parts: \begin{eqnarray*} & & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\ & & =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\}, \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon = 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\ & = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon \right\}\\ & - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]. \end{eqnarray*} We collect the above computations and obtain the following \begin{align*} & f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\ & -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\ & - 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B' - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^> \end{align*} where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$. We recall \begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim {\delta(\alpha^*)} . \end{equation} $\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}: $$ \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}, $$ $$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ by choosing $B$ large enough. By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small) \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} \\& \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2} \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp} $$ \left(\int q^4 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$, \begin{eqnarray*} && \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}} (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&- 20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \bigg|\\ && \lesssim B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left( |p|^2+|q|^2\right) (|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon| (|p|+|q|) \left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is $$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$ To estimate it, we note the following \begin{align*} &\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\ & \lesssim |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|). \end{align*} Now, using \begin{equation} \int |p| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, \quad \int |q_y| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}, \end{equation} we obtain proceeding as before \begin{align*} &\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon] \right|\\ &\lesssim \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{align*} We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$: \begin{eqnarray*} && \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\ &&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\ && +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\ && \lesssim \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}\\ && \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization (see more details in \cite{MMR1}) \begin{eqnarray*} & & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right| \\ &=& \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon -Z\right) Z \right|\\ & \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\ & \leq & \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}\right] +\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} $\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before. We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate: $$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, to control: \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6 -\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - First, using \eqref{weightedonebis}, \begin{align*} \frac 1 s\int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} & \lesssim \frac 1s \left( 1+ \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac {10}9}}\right) \mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}\\ & \lesssim s^{\frac {10}9 \beta -1}\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89} \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4}{B} \mathcal N_{2, \rm loc} + s^{10 \beta -9}. \end{align*} Second, using $\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc} \lesssim s^{-\frac 52 }$ and $\beta<\frac 78$, \begin{align*} \int_{y> \frac B2} \varepsilon^2 y\varphi_{i,B}' & \lesssim \left(\frac 1s + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} \right) \int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}\\ & \lesssim \left(\frac 1s + \mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \right) s^{\frac {10}9 \beta }\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89} \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4}{B} \mathcal N_{2, \rm loc} + s^{10 \beta -9}. \end{align*} {\bf step 5} $f_3^{(i)}$ term. \begin{align*} f_3^{(i)}&= 2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\ &+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon. \end{align*} First, $$ |(Q_b)_s|=\left|b_s P \left( \chi(|b|^{\gamma} y) + \gamma |b|^\gamma y \chi'(|b|^{\gamma} y)\right)\right|\lesssim |b_s| . $$ \begin{align*} &\left| \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\right| \\ & \lesssim |b_s|\int\psi_B \left(\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3+\delta(\alpha^*)) +|\varepsilon| (e^{-\frac {|y|}2} p^4+q^4) \right)\\ & \lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2} + \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}\right) \left( \int (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \psi_{B} + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 \psi_B \right)^{\frac 12 } \left( \int q^8\psi_B \right)^{\frac 12}\right)\\ & \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} For the next two terms, we first remark that by explicit computations: $$ \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s)^2\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Thus, as before, \begin{align*} & \left|\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \right| \\ & \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Finally, $$ \left| \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon \right| \lesssim \left( \int \psi_B (q_s q^4)^2 \right)^{\frac 12} \left( \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}\lesssim \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^4}. $$ \medskip {\bf step 6} Proof of {\rm (\ref{lowerbound})}. We proceed as in \cite{MMR1}. Recall that for $B$ large enough, $\mu>0$, $$\int \psi_B\varepsilon_y^2 + \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon^2- 5 \psi_B Q^4\varepsilon^2 \geq \mu \mathcal N_i.$$ We only have to estimate the error term as follows. For $s_0$ large enough, and $\alpha^*$ small enough, \begin{align*} & \left| \int \left( (Q_b{+}\varepsilon{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} 6 \varepsilon (Q_b^5 {+} q^5 {+} 5 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)) {-} 6 Q^4 \varepsilon^2\right) \psi_B\right| \\ & \lesssim \frac 1 {s^2}\left( \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1s \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \leq \frac \mu {10} \mathcal N_i+ \frac 1 {s^4} . \end{align*} This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{propasymtp}.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate s^j F_i, split into f_1, f_2, f_3 and estimate each region; the key step is the localized virial coercivity (Lemma B.1).

nodes.name: Localized virial estimate (Lemma B.1)
nodes.statement: There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that if $B\geq B_{0}$, then $$ \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) - \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}. $$
nodes.label: cl:9

nodes.name: Integrate the conserved quantity in s, introducing the const
nodes.statement: We now integrate explicitly {\rm (\ref{dynsyst})} and fit the parameters of the tail $(c_0,\theta)$ to obtain the blow up regimes described in Theorem \ref{th:1}. Integrating in $s$, we find $$ \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} =\ell_0, $$ where $\ell_0$ is a constant.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the conserved quantity in s, introducing the constant l_0

nodes.name: Restrict to the threshold l_0=0 and integrate again, introdu
nodes.statement: We focus on the threshold regime $\ell_0=0$ leading to: \begin{equation} \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}=0, \end{equation} which can now be integrated as follows: $$ \lambda^{-\frac 12}\lambda_s = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda x^{-\theta} = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 x_s x^{-\theta} $$ or equivalently after integration: $$ \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s) = \ell_1. $$
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the threshold l_0=0 and integrate again, introducing l_1

nodes.name: Restrict to the threshold l_1=0
nodes.statement: We focus again on the threshold regime $\ell_1=0$ leading to: $$ \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) = -\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s). $$
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the threshold l_1=0

nodes.name: Deduce c_0<0 and the ODE x_s = lambda
nodes.statement: We see that $c_0<0$ is necessary at this point and $$ x_s(s) = \lambda(s) = \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 x^{-2 \theta+2}(s). $$
nodes.statement_short: Deduce c_0<0 and the ODE x_s = lambda

nodes.name: Integrate to get x(s) and lambda(s) explicitly
nodes.statement: By integration on $[s_0,s]$, choosing $ x^{2\theta-1}(s_0)=(2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s_0$, we obtain $$ x^{2\theta-1}(s) = (2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s, $$ and thus $$ \lambda(s) = (2\theta- 1)^{\frac {-2\theta+2}{2\theta-1}} \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} \frac {1}{\theta-1} c_0\right)^{\frac {2}{2 \theta-1}} s^{- \frac {2(\theta-1)}{2\theta-1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get x(s) and lambda(s) explicitly

nodes.name: Implement for 0<beta<11/20 and return to original time
nodes.statement: \noindent (iv) \emph{Conclusion of the proof returning to the original time variable.} The above strategy is implemented for all $0<\beta<\frac{11}{20}$. Now we show how the behavior of the parameters {\rm (\ref{eq:blx})} (see the precise estimates in \eqref{sharp}) in renormalized time leads to the scenarios of Theorem \ref{th:1} in the original time $t$ (after possible scaling and time translation to adjust constants).
nodes.statement_short: Implement for 0<beta<11/20 and return to original time

nodes.name: Case 1/3<beta<11/20: finite integral of lambda^3 gives finit
nodes.statement:
oindent{-- Blow up in finite time:} for $  rac 13 <  eta <  rac {11}{20}. $ From \eqref{sharpintro}, {m (ef{eq:blx})}: $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\lambda^3(s)} ds=T<+\infty$$ and the solution $u(t)$ blows up in finite time $T$. Moreover, $$ T-t=\int_{s(t)}^{+\infty}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} \sim  rac {s^{ -( 3  eta-1)}}{3 eta-1} , \quad \lambda(t) \sim \left[ (3 eta-1)(T-t)ight]^{ rac { eta}{3 eta-1}}, $$ which implies $\|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \|Q'\|_{L^2} \lambda^{-1} (t) \sim C (T-t)^{-

nodes.name: Case beta=1/3: logarithmic time change gives exponential gro
nodes.statement: \noindent{-- Grow up in infinite time:} for $ \beta = \frac 13, $ the solution $u(t)$ is global in time since $\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} {\lambda^3(s)} ds =+\infty$. Moreover, for some $c_0$ and some $c_1 >0$, $$ t=\int_{s_0}^{s(t)}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} = {\rm log} s + c_0 +O(s^{-\frac 1{10}}),\quad s\sim c_1 e^t ,\quad \lambda(t)\sim c_1^{-\frac 13} e^{-\frac t 3} . $$ This means grow up in infinite time for $u(t)$ with exponential growth. Scaling and time translation lead to any exponential rate $e^{-ct}$, $c>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case beta=1/3: logarithmic time change gives exponential grow up

nodes.name: Case beta<1/3: power grow up t^nu
nodes.statement: Finally, for $0<\beta< \frac 13,$ we also obtain a global solution $u(t)$ since $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \lambda^3(s) ds \geq 2^{-3} \int_{s_0}^{+\infty} s^{-3 \beta} ds = +\infty,$$ and $$t= \int_{s_0}^{t(s)} \lambda^3(s') ds' \sim \frac 1{1-3 \beta} s^{1-3 \beta} , \quad \lambda(t) \sim (1-3 \beta)^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}} t^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}} , $$ which means grow up rates $t^\nu$ at $+\infty$, for any $\nu=\frac {\beta}{1-3\beta}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case beta<1/3: power grow up t^nu

nodes.name: Existence of Y_0 from standard properties of L
nodes.statement: Note that the existence and uniqueness of $Y_0$ follows readily from standard properties of the operator $L$ (see e.g. \cite{MMR1}). Moreover, $$ (Q,Y_0)= -\frac 12 (L\Lambda Q,Y_0) =-\frac 12(\Lambda Q,5Q^4 ) =-\frac 34 \int Q^5=-\frac 34 \int Q. $$
nodes.statement_short: Existence of Y_0 from standard properties of L; compute (Q,Y_0)

nodes.name: Part (ii) quoted from MMR1
nodes.statement: Part (ii) is taken from \cite{MMR1}, Proposition 2.2.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii) quoted from MMR1

nodes.name: Step 1: decomposition
nodes.statement: {\bf step 1} Proof of (i). This is a standard modulation claim. As usual, the decomposition is first performed for a fixed time $t$. For $t\in [0,t_0]$ fixed, define the map $$ \Theta: (\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w,z_0) \mapsto \left( \int Q\bar \varepsilon , \int \Lambda Q \bar \varepsilon ,\int Q' \bar \varepsilon \right), $$ where $x_0=1/z_0$, $$ \bar \varepsilon(y)=\varepsilon_{(\bar b,{\bar \lambda},\bar x,w_1,z_0)}(y) = {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12} w_1\left(t, {\bar \lambda} y + \bar x\right) - {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12} {\lambda_1^{\frac 12}(t)} q_0\left(t,x_1(t) + \bar x\right)Y_0(y)- Q_{\bar b}(y), $$ $$ w_1(t,y)= { \lambda_1(t)}^{\frac 12} w \left(t, {\lambda_1(t)} y + x_1(t)\right)=Q(y)+\varepsilon_1(t,y). $$ We have $\bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}=0,$ so that $\Theta(0,1,0,Q,0)=0$ and $$ \quad \partial_{\bar b} \bar \varepsilon |_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= P, \quad \partial_{\bar \lambda} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= \Lambda Q, \quad \partial_{\bar x} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= Q'. $$ so that differentiating the map $\Theta$ with respect to the variables $(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x)$ at the point $(0,1,0,Q,0)$ we find the Jacobian matrix $$ \left(\begin{array}{ ccc } (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & (P,Q') \\ (\Lambda Q,Q) & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) & (\Lambda Q,Q') \\ (Q',Q) & (Q',\lambda Q) & (Q',Q')\\ \end{array}\right)= \left(\begin{array}{ ccc } (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & 0\\0 & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) &0 \\ 0 & 0 & (Q',Q')\\ \end{array}\right), $$ which is not degenerate since $(P,Q)>0$. It follows from these observations that we can apply the implicit function theorem to $\Theta$: for $w_1$ small and $x_0$ large, there exists a unique $(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)=(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)(w_1,x_0)$ close to $(0,1,0)$ such that $\Theta(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w_1,\tfrac 1{x_0})=0$. Then, we define $b(t)=\bar b(w_1(t),x_0)$, $\lambda(t)=\bar \lambda(w_1(t),x_0) \lambda_1(t)$, $x(t)=\bar x(w_1(t),x_0)+x_1(t)$ and $\varepsilon(t)=\bar \varepsilon(t)$. The regularity of $(b(t),\lambda(t),x(t))$ now follow from standard arguments. It follows that we have the following decomposition of $u(t,x)$: \begin{align} u(t,x) & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \\ & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Construct the decomposition by the implicit function theorem

nodes.statement: Second, set $ \varepsilon_Y(s,y)= p(s) Y_0(y) +\varepsilon(s,y)$ so that $$ w(s,x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}(s)} \left( Q_{b(s)} + \varepsilon_Y \right)\left(s,\frac {x-x(s)}{\lambda(s)}\right). $$ By standard computations, we obtain for $\varepsilon_Y$: \begin{align} \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon_Y & = (-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon_Y + \varepsilon_Y - (\varepsilon_Y+Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5)_y - (5 Q^4 q)_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon_Y \\ & + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b + \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon_Y)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y, \end{align} where $$ W=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon_Y)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^3 q^2 + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y) q^4. $$

nodes.name: Step 3: conservation laws
nodes.statement: {\bf step 3} Estimates induced by the conservation laws. By $L^2$ norm conservation, \begin{align*} & \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2 = \int Q_b^2 - \int Q^2 + \int (\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^2 + 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 +q) Q_b\\ &= 2 b(P,Q) + O(|b|^{2-\gamma}) +\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2 + O(|b|^{1-\frac \gamma 2}\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}) +O(|p|+ \|q\|_{L^2}). \end{align*} Estimate \eqref{twobound} follows. By energy conservation, $Q''+Q^5= Q$ and $\int \varepsilon Q=0$, \begin{align*} & 2 \lambda^2 E(u_0) = 2 E(Q_b + \varepsilon + pY_0 +q) \\& = 2 E(Q_b) - 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q) \left( (Q_b-Q)_{yy}+ (Q_b^5 - Q^5) \right) - 2 \int (pY_0 + q) Q \\ &+ \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)_y^2 - \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6 Q_b^5(\varepsilon+pY+q)\right)\\ & = - 2 b (P,Q) + O(b^2) + O\left( |b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right)\right) - 2 p \left( \int Y_0 Q + \int Q\right) \\ &+ 2 \int (p-q) Q + \|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2 + O(p^2) + O\left(\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}(|p|+ \|q_y\|_{L^2})\right) + 2\lambda^2 E(q_0) \\ &- \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5 (\varepsilon+pY_0+q) -q^6\right) \end{align*} By \eqref{YQ}, we have $\int Y_0 Q + \int Q = \frac 14 \int Q$. Using in addition \eqref{PQ}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{cl.1bis}, we obtain \begin{align*} \frac 1{\lambda^2}\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + \frac p{\lambda^2}\right| + \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+ \frac {|b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma}}{\lambda^2} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right) \\ & + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x} + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}\\ & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right| + \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+ \frac { |p| }{x^2} + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x} + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of the refined law (fond)
nodes.statement:
\emph{Proof of \eqref{fond}.} First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7. Recall from \cite{MMR1}, $$(\Psi_b,Q)= - rac {b^2}{8} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 + O(|b|^3),\quad (\Phi_b, Q) = - rac {b_s}{16} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 +O(|b|^{10}). $$ Note also that from direct computations and parity properties  egin{align*} &\left|\left( ((\varepsilon+pY_0 + Q_b)^5 - Q_b^5 - p5Q^4 Y_0 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon)_y,Qight) - 20 bp((Q^3Y_0 P )_y,Q) ight| \ &+ \left| \left((\widetilde W)_y,Qight)-20 bp (( P Q^3)_y,Q)ight|\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} . \end{align*} (See \cite{MMR1} for details on the nonlinear terms in $\varepsilon$.) Using \eqref{cl.4bis} and the above estimates we find egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (Y_0,Q) -  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) 
onumber\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] + c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg) igg|\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} + rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+ rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|. \end{align} We claim the following cancellation  egin{equation} - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0. \end{equation} Indeed, $L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$ and so from \eqref{eq:23},  egin{align*} & - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)- 20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\ & = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') -  rac 12 \int Q \ & = - \int P' -  rac 12 \int Q = P(-\infty) -  rac 12 \int Q =0. \end{align*} Thus,  egin{align*} & \left| -  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] ight| = |p| \left|  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b ight| |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|. \end{align*} \medskip Now, from $(Y_0,Q) =-  rac 34 \int Q$ (see \eqref{YQ}), using \eqref{cl.1bis} and \eqref{cl.2bis} we note that  egin{align} &  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg)
onumber \ & =  rac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 12  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + rac 	heta 3  rac {x_s}{x} ight) +O\left( rac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|ight) + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left| rac{x_s}{\lambda}-1ight|ight). \end{align} Therefore,  egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight)  igg| 
onumber \ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} +  rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| +  rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| . \end{align} Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation, $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac 4{\left(\int Qight)}c_0 	heta \lambda^{- rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta}ight) = -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{- rac 32} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight) $$ $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac b{\lambda^2}ight) =  rac {b_s}{\lambda^2} - 2  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}  rac b{\lambda^2} =  rac {b_s}{\lambda^2} + 2  rac {b^2}{\lambda^2} - 2 \left(  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +bight)  rac b{\lambda^2}.$$ and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.
nodes.statement_short: Proof of the refined law (fond)

nodes.name: Refined equation for b_s by projecting on Q
nodes.statement: First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7. Recall from \cite{MMR1}, $$(\Psi_b,Q)= -\frac {b^2}{8} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 + O(|b|^3),\quad (\Phi_b, Q) = -\frac {b_s}{16} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 +O(|b|^{10}). $$ Note also that from direct computations and parity properties \begin{align*} &\left|\left( ((\varepsilon+pY_0 + Q_b)^5 - Q_b^5 - p5Q^4 Y_0 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon)_y,Q\right) - 20 bp((Q^3Y_0 P )_y,Q) \right| \\ &+ \left| \left((\widetilde W)_y,Q\right)-20 bp (( P Q^3)_y,Q)\right|\\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} . \end{align*} (See \cite{MMR1} for details on the nonlinear terms in $\varepsilon$.) Using \eqref{cl.4bis} and the above estimates we find\begin{align} &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q) - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) \nonumber\\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right] + c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\bigg|\\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} +\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Refined equation for b_s by projecting on Q

nodes.name: Algebraic cancellation (cancel) and its consequence
nodes.statement: We claim the following cancellation \begin{equation} - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0. \end{equation} Indeed, $L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$ and so from \eqref{eq:23}, \begin{align*} & - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \\ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)- 20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\\ & = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') - \frac 12 \int Q \\ & = - \int P' - \frac 12 \int Q = P(-\infty) - \frac 12 \int Q =0. \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} & \left| - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right] \right| = |p| \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b \right| |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Algebraic cancellation (cancel) and its consequence

nodes.name: Verify the cancellation using the equation of P
nodes.statement: Indeed, $L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$ and so from \eqref{eq:23}, \begin{align*} & - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \\ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)- 20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\\ & = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') - \frac 12 \int Q \\ & = - \int P' - \frac 12 \int Q = P(-\infty) - \frac 12 \int Q =0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Verify the cancellation using the equation of P

nodes.name: The p terms reduce to |p||lambda_s/lambda + b|
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} & \left| - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right] \right| = |p| \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b \right| |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The p terms reduce to |p||lambda_s/lambda + b|

nodes.name: Compute the tail contribution and obtain (eq:b)
nodes.statement: Now, from $(Y_0,Q) =- \frac 34 \int Q$ (see \eqref{YQ}), using \eqref{cl.1bis} and \eqref{cl.2bis} we note that \begin{align} & \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\nonumber \\ & = \frac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +\frac \theta 3 \frac {x_s}{x} \right) +O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|\right) + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\right). \end{align} Therefore, \begin{align} &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + \theta \frac {x_s}{x} \right) \bigg| \nonumber \\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the tail contribution and obtain (eq:b)

nodes.name: Differentiate b/lambda^2 + tail term and conclude
nodes.statement: Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation, $$ \frac d{ds}\left( \frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}\right) = - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + \theta \frac {x_s}{x} \right) $$ $$ \frac d{ds}\left( \frac b{\lambda^2}\right) = \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2} - 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \frac b{\lambda^2} = \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2} + 2 \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2} - 2 \left( \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right) \frac b{\lambda^2}.$$ and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate b/lambda^2 + tail term and conclude

nodes.name: Bounds on q from conservation laws of q_0
nodes.statement: {\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$, $$ \|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\quad E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-\theta- \frac 12}, $$ and \eqref{L2H1q} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on q from conservation laws of q_0

nodes.name: Properties of p
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, \eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$. Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz}, splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|< rac {x(s)}{4}$ and $\lambda |y| >  rac {x(s)}{4}$, we have  egin{align} & e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}. \end{align} Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},  egin{align*} &\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Qight) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y \ &= -\lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\ &= - \lambda^{ rac 32} f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5 - \lambda^{ rac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))ight)dy \ & -\lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))ight) dy\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( \lambda^{ rac 32}e^{- rac 54 x(s) } ight) + O\left( \lambda^{ rac 52} x^{-	heta-2}ight) +O\left( \lambda^{ rac 32} x^{-	heta-3}(s)ight)\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| ight) + O\left( rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| ight), \end{align*} where we have split the integrals above into $|y| > rac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|>  rac 34 x(s) >  rac 12 t +  rac 12 x_0$, so that \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {m (ef{cl.4bis})} is proved.\ Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By explicit differentiation and Lemma ef{le:qz},  egin{align*} p_s -  rac 12  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = \lambda^{ rac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{ rac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\ & = \lambda^{ rac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{ rac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s)) + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight)\ & = -	heta  rac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight). \end{align*} Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (| rac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Properties of p

nodes.name: Approximation of p from the tail asymptotics
nodes.statement: Since $p(s) = \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, \eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximation of p from the tail asymptotics

nodes.name: Localized bound on p - q by splitting space
nodes.statement:
Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz}, splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|< rac {x(s)}{4}$ and $\lambda |y| >  rac {x(s)}{4}$, we have  egin{align} & e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Localized bound on p - q by splitting space

nodes.name: Leading tail interaction term (cl.4bis)
nodes.statement: Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}, \begin{align*} &\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y \\ &= -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\\ &= - \lambda^{\frac 32} f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5 - \lambda^{\frac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))\right)dy \\ & -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))\right) dy\\ & =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta -1}(s) + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32}e^{-\frac 54 x(s) } \right) + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 52} x^{-\theta-2}\right) +O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32} x^{-\theta-3}(s)\right)\\ & =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta -1}(s) + O\left(\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| \right) + O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| \right), \end{align*} where we have split the integrals above into $|y| >\frac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|> \frac 34 x(s) > \frac 12 t + \frac 12 x_0$, so that \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {\rm (\ref{cl.4bis})} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Leading tail interaction term (cl.4bis)

nodes.name: Differentiate p to get (cl.2bis)
nodes.statement: Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By explicit differentiation and Lemma \ref{le:qz}, \begin{align*} p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = \lambda^{\frac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\\ & = \lambda^{\frac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s)) + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right) \right)\\ & = -\theta \frac {x_s} x |p| + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right) \right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate p to get (cl.2bis)

nodes.name: Deduce (cl.2tri)
nodes.statement: Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce (cl.2tri)

nodes.name: Remainder estimates for W
nodes.statement: {\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note \begin{align*} \widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p Y_0)^4 - Q^4\right] (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0) (p^4-q^4). \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} & \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W| \\ &\lesssim \left( |p|+|b| \right) \int e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}} |p-q| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}} |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & + \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\lambda}{x}|p|, \end{align*} using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate $$ e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}. $$ Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that $p^2$ appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: Remainder estimates for W

nodes.name: Expand W - tilde W
nodes.statement: For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note \begin{align*} \widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p Y_0)^4 - Q^4\right] (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0) (p^4-q^4). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand W - tilde W

nodes.name: Bound using (cl.2)
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} & \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W| \\ &\lesssim \left( |p|+|b| \right) \int e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}} |p-q| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}} |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & + \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\lambda}{x}|p|, \end{align*} using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate $$ e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound using (cl.2)

nodes.name: Parity and direct estimates for (cl.4), (cl.5)
nodes.statement: Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that $p^2$ appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: Parity and direct estimates for (cl.4), (cl.5)

nodes.name: Identify the initial parameters by uniqueness of the decompo
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS}. First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that $$ b_0=b(s_0),\quad \lambda(s_0)=\lambda_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \varepsilon(s_0)=\varepsilon_0. $$
nodes.statement_short: Identify the initial parameters by uniqueness of the decomposition

nodes.name: Assume the exit time s* is finite for all data in D
nodes.statement: We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$, we have $$ s^*(\lambda_0,b_0) := \mathop{\rm sup} \left\{ s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$} \right\} <+\infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume the exit time s* is finite for all data in D

nodes.name: Plan: close bootstrap, then topology
nodes.statement: We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\lambda_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: close bootstrap, then topology

nodes.name: Case beta > 1/3: t(s) < 1
nodes.statement: Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right) <1 $$ for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Case beta > 1/3: t(s) < 1
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Case beta = 1/3: x(t) grows faster than t^3
nodes.statement: For $\beta = \frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, {\rm log}\frac s{s_0} \quad \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}. $$ Thus, $$ x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 . $$ for $s_0$ large enough. Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^3 + \frac 12 x_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case beta = 1/3: x(t) grows faster than t^3
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Case beta < 1/3
nodes.statement: Finally, for $0<\beta <\frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right) $$ so that for $s_0$ large $$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}}, $$ and $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15 t^{1+\beta}.$$ Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case beta < 1/3
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Bound on p
nodes.statement: The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that $$ 0< p \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound on p
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Remaining bounds from the modulation equations
nodes.statement: The estimates \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are immediate consequences of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remaining bounds from the modulation equations
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Integrate the tail monotonicity
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), $$ \frac d{ds} \left\{ \lambda^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2 \right\} \lesssim \lambda^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} + s^{-2}\right) \lesssim s^{-10 \beta -2}, $$ so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2}, $$ \lambda^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s) \leq \lambda^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10\beta} \leq 2. $$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the tail monotonicity

nodes.name: Closed weighted tail bound (aa3)
nodes.statement: By the properties of $\varphi_{10}$ and \eqref{A2}, we obtain \begin{equation} \lambda^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \varepsilon^2(s,y) dy \leq 3. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Closed weighted tail bound (aa3)

nodes.name: Apply the Lyapunov control with j=5/2
nodes.statement: Now, we apply Lemma \ref{propasymtp} with $j=\frac 52 $. We find by \eqref{lyapounovconrolbis} and $\beta< \frac {11}{20}$, \begin{equation} \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Lyapunov control with j=5/2

nodes.name: Integrate in time
nodes.statement: The initial smallness {\rm (\ref{A2})} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of {\rm (\ref{neovneogbgeo})} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields: $$ \mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} $$ for some $\delta=\delta(\beta)>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate in time

nodes.name: Coercivity closes N_i
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude: $$ \mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq \frac 12 s^{- \frac 52} $$ for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws {\rm (\ref{twobound})}, {\rm (\ref{energbound})} concludes the proof of (BS3').
nodes.statement_short: Coercivity closes N_i

nodes.name: Decay of g_s, lambda_s/lambda + b, x_s/lambda - 1
nodes.statement: First, note that from \eqref{fond}, \eqref{eq:2002bis}, and using (BS2)-(BS3), $\frac 13 \leq \beta\leq \frac 9{10}$, we have on $[s_0,s^*]$: \begin{equation} \left| g_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 9 4 + 2 \beta }, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + b \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 54}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1 \right|\lesssim s^{-\frac 54}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Decay of g_s, lambda_s/lambda + b, x_s/lambda - 1

nodes.name: lambda close to the tail law in x via the bound on f
