nodes.statement: By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1-\beta)(\theta-1) =\frac \beta 2$ the estimate: \begin{align} & \left| \lambda (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &= \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \lambda^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: lambda close to the tail law in x via the bound on f

nodes.name: ODE for x^{1/(1-beta)}
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{dx}, we find $$ \left| x_s (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}} + s^{-\frac 54 - \beta } \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}. $$ and hence\begin{equation} \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} from $2\theta-1=\frac 1{1-\beta}$ and the choice of $c_0$ in {\rm (\ref{defcobeta})} which gives: $$ (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)}= (2\theta-1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2. $$
nodes.statement_short: ODE for x^{1/(1-beta)}

nodes.name: Integrate to get the asymptotics of x
nodes.statement: Since from {\rm (\ref{initixzero})}: $$ \frac {(1-\beta) }{s_0^{1-\beta}} x (s_0)= 1,$$ the time integration of {\rm (\ref{vnkrvrnorn})} on $[s_0,s]$ yields $$ \left|x^{\frac 1{\beta-1}}(s) - (1-\beta)^{-\frac 1{\beta-1}} s \right| \lesssim s^{1-\frac 1{10}}. $$ Thus, \begin{equation} \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to get the asymptotics of x

nodes.name: Asymptotics of lambda
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{aa2} into \eqref{bbb2}, we find for $\lambda$, \begin{equation} \left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotics of lambda

nodes.name: Asymptotics of b and conclusion
nodes.statement: Finally, using $|g(s)| \leq s^{-1 + 2 \beta - \frac 1{5}}$, we find \begin{equation} \left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} From \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2}, (BS2') follows for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotics of b and conclusion

nodes.name: Reduce to closing (BS1) by choice of initial parameters
nodes.statement: We now claim from a standard topological argument based on the ougoing behavior of the ODE's for $(f,g)$ that we can find $(b_0,\lambda_0)\in \mathcal D$ such that the remaining condition $(BS1)$ is closed.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to closing (BS1) by choice of initial parameters
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Introduce rescaled F, G and H = F^2 + G^2
nodes.statement: Indeed, let $$ G(s) = g(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},\quad F(s) = f(s) s^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}, $$ and $$ H(s) = F^2(s) + G^2(s). $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce rescaled F, G and H = F^2 + G^2
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: At exit time H(s*)=1
nodes.statement: From (BS2') and (BS3'), since $s^*=s^*(x_0,b_0)<+\infty$, it follows from a standard continuity argument that at $s=s^* \geq s_0,$ \begin{equation} H(s^*)=1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: At exit time H(s*)=1
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Strict outgoing behavior H'(s*) >= 1/(20 s*)
nodes.statement: We first claim the strict outgoing behavior: \begin{equation} H'(s^*)\geq \frac {1}{20 s^*}. \end{equation} \emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.} Since $$ G'(s) = \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) g(s)s^{-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}} +g'(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}}, $$ we have using {\rm (\ref{dFdG})}: \begin{equation} G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*} +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right). \end{equation} Similarly, $$ F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1} + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}. $$ We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx} and (BS1)-(BS2), \begin{align*} f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 x_s x^{-\theta} \\ & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[ \frac b{\lambda^2} - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right] +O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\ &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) = O\left(s^{-1 -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right). \end{align*} Thus, \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). \end{equation} Therefore $$ H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right) \geq \frac 1{20s^*}, $$ for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Strict outgoing behavior H'(s*) >= 1/(20 s*)
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Derivative of G at s*
nodes.statement: \emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.} Since $$ G'(s) = \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) g(s)s^{-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}} +g'(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}}, $$ we have using {\rm (\ref{dFdG})}: \begin{equation} G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*} +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Derivative of G at s*
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Derivative of F
nodes.statement: Similarly, $$ F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1} + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Derivative of F
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: f' is small, controlled by g
nodes.statement: We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx} and (BS1)-(BS2), \begin{align*} f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 x_s x^{-\theta} \\ & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[ \frac b{\lambda^2} - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right] +O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\ &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) = O\left(s^{-1 -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: f' is small, controlled by g
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Derivative of F at s*
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Derivative of F at s*
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Combine to get H'(s*) > 0
nodes.statement: Therefore $$ H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right) \geq \frac 1{20s^*}, $$ for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get H'(s*) > 0
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Outgoing behavior makes the exit time continuous
nodes.statement: By standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}), the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$ is continuous.
nodes.statement_short: Outgoing behavior makes the exit time continuous
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Parametrize initial data by (F_0,G_0) in the unit disc
nodes.statement: We define the continuous maps \begin{align*} \lambda_0(F_0) &= s_0^{-\beta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}} \right)^2 \\ b_0(F_0,G_0) &= \beta s_0^{-1+\frac \beta 2} \lambda_0^{\frac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{\frac 32\beta - \frac 1{5}} \lambda_0^{\frac 32} (F_0) \right)\\ & = \beta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right| \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{- \frac 1{5}} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|^3 \right) \end{align*} so that \begin{align*} G_0 &= s_0^{1-2 \beta +\frac 1{5}} \left( \frac {b_0}{\lambda_0^2} - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0 \lambda_0^{-\frac 32} x_0^{-\theta}\right)\\ F_0 &= s_0^{\frac \beta 2 +\frac 1{10}} \left( \lambda_0^{\frac 12} +\frac 2{\int Q} c_0 \frac 1{\theta-1} x_0^{-\theta+1} \right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize initial data by (F_0,G_0) in the unit disc
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: The exit map is a retraction of the disc onto the circle, co
nodes.statement: Now, consider the continous map \begin{align*} \mathcal M \ : \ \ \ \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2} &\to \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\ (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right). \end{align*} where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have $\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, $\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map $\mathcal M$ is in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem.
nodes.statement_short: The exit map is a retraction of the disc onto the circle, contradicting Brouwer
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Some initial parameters give global bootstrap and (sharp)
nodes.statement: Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that \begin{equation} | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\ Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\ This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}.
nodes.statement_short: Some initial parameters give global bootstrap and (sharp)
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Recall the definition of q_0 and f_0
nodes.statement: Recall that $c_0\in \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta>1$ are fixed, $x_0\gg 1$ is to be taken large enough and $q_0$ is the solution of \begin{equation} \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad q_0(0,x)= f_0(x), \end{equation} where the function $f_0$ is smooth and satisfies \begin{equation} f_0(x)= c_0 x^{-\theta} \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\quad f_0(x)=0 \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \hbox{ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$, for all $k\geq 0$},\quad \left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim c_0 |x|^{-\theta - k}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the definition of q_0 and f_0

nodes.name: Small data Cauchy theory gives global bounded q_0
nodes.statement: First, for $x_0$ large enough, $\|f_0\|_{L^2}$ is small and it follows from the $L^2$ and $H^s$ Cauchy theory (Corollary 2.9 in \cite{KPV}) that $q_0$ is global and bounded in $H^s$ for all $s\geq 0$, with $$\mathop{\rm sup}_t\|q_0(t)\|_{H^s}\lesssim \delta(x_0^{-1}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Small data Cauchy theory gives global bounded q_0

nodes.name: Define q_1 = q_0 - f_0 and its equation
nodes.statement: We define $$ q_1(t,x) = q_0(t,x) -f_0(x), $$ \begin{equation} \partial_t q_1 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1+f_0)^5-f_0^5)=F_0,\quad q_1(0,x)= 0, \end{equation} where $$ F_0 = -\partial_x^3 f_0 - \partial_x(f_0^5). $$
nodes.statement_short: Define q_1 = q_0 - f_0 and its equation

nodes.name: Weights moving at speed 1/4 and weighted functionals M, E, F
nodes.statement: For any $\bar \theta\geq 0$, define a smooth function $\varphi_{\bar \theta}$ such that \begin{equation} \varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) = x^{\bar \theta} \text{ for $x\geq 4$},\quad \varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) = e^{\frac x8} \text{ for $x\leq 0$},\quad \varphi'\geq 0,\ \varphi'''\leq \frac 14 \varphi' \text{ on $\mathbb{R}$}. \end{equation} For $$ 0\leq \theta_1< 2 \theta+4, \quad \theta_1 \neq 2 \theta+3, $$ set \begin{align*} M_{\theta_1}(t)& = \int q_1^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) dx, \\ E_{\theta_1}(t) &= \int \left( (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right) \right)\varphi_{\theta_1+2}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 \right) dx,\\\ F_{\theta_1,k}(t) &= \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) dx, \ k\geq 2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Weights moving at speed 1/4 and weighted functionals M, E, F

nodes.name: Weighted mass estimate (eqM)
nodes.statement: We differentiate $M_{\theta_1}(t)$ (omitting the variable $x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4$ for the function $\varphi_{\theta_1}$): \begin{align*} M_{\theta_1}'(t) & = - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 14 \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' + \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}''' \\ & + 2 \int \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) (q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1})_x + 2 \left|\int F_0 q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1} \right|\\ & \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 3{16} \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' - 2 \int \left[ \frac {(q_1+f_0)^6}6 - \frac {f_0^6} 6-(q_1+f_0)^5 q_1\right] \varphi_{\theta_1}' \\ & + 2 \int \left[ (q_1+f_0)^5 - 5 q_1^4 f_0-f_0^5\right] f_0' \varphi_{\theta_1} + 2 \left|\int F_0^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'} \right|^{\frac 12} \left| \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'\right|^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 1 8 \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' +\delta(x_0^{-1}) \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' + C \int F_0^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'} . \end{align*} Thus, for $x_0$ large enough, we have obtained $$ M_{\theta_1}'(t) + \frac 1{10} \int \left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2 + q_1^2 \right] \varphi_{\theta_1}' \lesssim \int F_0^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'} . $$ For $x_0$ large enough, \begin{align} \int F_0^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2} {\varphi_{\theta_1}'}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) & \lesssim \int_{x>\frac t4 + \frac {x_0} 4 + 4} x^{-2(\theta+3)} \left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 \right)^{\theta_1+1} \nonumber \\ & + \int_{\frac t8 + \frac {x_0} 8 < x<\frac t4 + \frac {x_0} 4 + 4} x^{-2(\theta+3)} +\int_{x< \frac t8 + \frac {x_0} 8} e^{\frac 18 (x-\frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 )}\nonumber \\ & \lesssim (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-4 } . \end{align} Therefore, using also $M_{\theta_1}(0)=0$, we find by integration: \begin{equation} M_{\theta_1}(t) + \int_0^t\int \left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2 + q_1^2 \right] \varphi_{\theta_1}' \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Weighted mass estimate (eqM)

nodes.name: Weighted energy estimate (eqE)
nodes.statement: We argue similarly for $E_{\theta_1}(t)$. \begin{align*} E_{\theta_1}'(t) & = 2 \int \partial_t q_1 \left[ - \partial_x^2 q_1 - \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right)\right] \varphi_{\theta_1+2}\\ & - 2 \int \partial_t q_1 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' - \frac 14 \int\left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right) \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}' \\ &= - \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \right]^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\\ & - 2 \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right] F_0\varphi_{\theta_1+2}\\ & + 2 \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right]_x \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' - 2 \int F_0 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' \\ &- \frac 14 \int\left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right) \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'. \end{align*} We use the following computations and estimates \begin{align*} &\left| \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right] F_0\varphi_{\theta_1+2} \right| \\ & \lesssim \left| \int \partial_x q_1 (F_0 \varphi_{\theta_1+2})_x \right| + \left| \int \left[ (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right] F_0\varphi_{\theta_1+2}\right| \\ & \lesssim \frac 1{100} \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' +\frac 1{100} \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' \\ & + C \int \left(|\partial_x F_0|^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'} + |F_0|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' + |F_0|^2 \frac {f_0^8 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'}\right). \end{align*} \begin{align*} 2 \int \partial_x^3 q_1 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' & = - 2 \int (\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' + \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'''\\ & \leq - 2 \int (\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' + \frac 14 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'. \end{align*} \begin{align*} & \left| 2 \int \left[ (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right]_x \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' \right|\\ & =\left| 10 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 (q_1+f_0)^4 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' +10 \int \left( (q_1+f_0)^4 - f_0^4\right) \partial_x f_0 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\right|\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+1}' + C \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'. \end{align*} \begin{align*} 2 \left| \int F_0 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\right| \leq \frac 1{100} \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+1}' + C \int |F_0|^2\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'. \end{align*} Combining these estimates, and using the expression of $F_0$ as in \eqref{Fzero}, we find \begin{align*} E_{\theta_1}'(t) \leq - \int (\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' - \frac 1{10} \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' + C\int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' + C (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-4 }. \end{align*} By integration, and using \eqref{eqM}, \begin{align} & E_{\theta_1}(t) + \frac 1{10} \int_0^t \int \left[(\partial_x^2 q_1)^2 + (\partial_x q_1)^2 \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\nonumber \\ & \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Weighted energy estimate (eqE)

nodes.name: Coercivity of E gives the weighted H^1 bound (eqEbb)
nodes.statement_short: Coercivity of E gives the weighted H^1 bound (eqEbb)

nodes.name: Pointwise decay of q_1 (A11)
nodes.statement: Note also that for any $x$, \begin{align} q_1^2(t,x) \varphi_{\theta_1+1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) & \lesssim \int_x^{+\infty} |q_1| |\partial_x q_1| \varphi_{\theta_1+1} +\int_x^{+\infty} |q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+1}' \nonumber \\ & \lesssim \int |\partial_x q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2} +\int |q_1|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1} , \end{align} and, with $\theta_1 = 2 \theta+ \frac {15}4$, using the properties of $\varphi_{\theta_1+1}$, for $x>\frac 12 (t+x_0)$, \begin{equation} |q_1(t,x)| \lesssim x^{- (\frac {\theta_1}2 +\frac 12 )} t^{\frac 38} =x^{- (\theta+\frac {19}8)} t^{\frac 38} \lesssim x^{- (\theta+2)}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise decay of q_1 (A11)

nodes.name: Higher derivatives by induction on k
nodes.statement: Finally, we briefly treat the case of higher order derivatives. We use an induction argument, assuming at the rank $k$ that for all $1\leq k'<k$, for all $x$, $t$ \begin{align}\nonumber & \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' \left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) dt + \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1(t))^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \\ & +|\partial_x^{k'-1} q_1(t)|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} \end{align} we prove the same estimates for $k'=k$ using $F_{\theta_1,k}$. Indeed, by simple computation: \begin{align*} F_{\theta_1,k}'(t) & = 2 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)_t (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} - \frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\ & = - 2 \int (\partial_x^{k+3} q_1) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} - 2 \int \partial_x^{k+1} \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 -f_0^5\right) \partial_x^k q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}\\ & - \frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \\ & \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' - \frac 14 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\ & + 2 \int \partial_x^k \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \left( (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} + (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\right) \\ & + \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}. \end{align*} We claim, arguing as \eqref{Fzero}, $$ \left| \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \right| \leq \frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ C t^{\theta_1-2 \theta -4}. $$ Next, we claim \begin{align} & \left|\int \partial_x^k \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \left( (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} + (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\right)\right|\nonumber \\ & \leq \frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^{k} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\sum_{k'=0}^{k-1} \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' . \end{align} Indeed, looking for example at the purely nonlinear term in $q_1$, we have \begin{align*} &\left|\int \partial_x^k (q_1^5) (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \right| + \left|\int \partial_x^k (q_1^5) (\partial_x^{k} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' \right| \\ &\leq C \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'} + \frac 1{200}\int (\partial_x^{k} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\frac 1{200} \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' , \end{align*} and \begin{align*} & \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'} \lesssim \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+ 2 k_1+2k_2+2k_3+2k_4+2k_5+1}\\ & \lesssim \sum_{ \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{2}{k_1+k_2+k_3+k_4+k_5=k}{k_5\geq k_4\geq k_3\geq k_2\geq k_1} } \left( \Pi_{l=1}^3 \| (\partial_x^{k_l} q_1 )^2 {\varphi_{2k_l+2}} \|_{L^\infty} \right) \| (\partial_x^{k_4} q_1 )^2 {\varphi_{2k_4-2}} \|_{L^\infty}\int |\partial_x^{k_5} q_1|^2\varphi'_{\theta_1+2k_5-1} \\ & \lesssim \delta(x_0^{-1})\sum_{k'=0}^k \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}'. \end{align*} where the $L^\infty$ norms above are estimated using \eqref{ply2}. The other terms, all containing $f_0$, are similar and easier. By integration of $F'_k$ using \eqref{ply3} and \eqref{ply2}, we obtain $$ F_{\theta_1,k}(t) + \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} $$ Arguing as in the proof of \eqref{linfty}, we prove \eqref{ply2} for $k'=k$. The induction argument being complete, we finish the proof as in \eqref{A11}.
nodes.statement_short: Higher derivatives by induction on k

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis (ply2) at rank k
nodes.statement: Finally, we briefly treat the case of higher order derivatives. We use an induction argument, assuming at the rank $k$ that for all $1\leq k'<k$, for all $x$, $t$ \begin{align}\nonumber & \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' \left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) dt + \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1(t))^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \\ & +|\partial_x^{k'-1} q_1(t)|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} \end{align} we prove the same estimates for $k'=k$ using $F_{\theta_1,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction hypothesis (ply2) at rank k

nodes.name: Differentiate F_{theta_1,k}
nodes.statement: Indeed, by simple computation: \begin{align*} F_{\theta_1,k}'(t) & = 2 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)_t (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} - \frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\ & = - 2 \int (\partial_x^{k+3} q_1) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} - 2 \int \partial_x^{k+1} \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 -f_0^5\right) \partial_x^k q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}\\ & - \frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \\ & \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' - \frac 14 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\ & + 2 \int \partial_x^k \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \left( (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} + (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\right) \\ & + \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate F_{theta_1,k}

nodes.name: Source term bound
nodes.statement: We claim, arguing as \eqref{Fzero}, $$ \left| \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \right| \leq \frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ C t^{\theta_1-2 \theta -4}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Source term bound

nodes.name: Nonlinear term bound (ply3)
nodes.statement: Next, we claim \begin{align} & \left|\int \partial_x^k \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \left( (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} + (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\right)\right|\nonumber \\ & \leq \frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^{k} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\sum_{k'=0}^{k-1} \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' . \end{align} Indeed, looking for example at the purely nonlinear term in $q_1$, we have \begin{align*} &\left|\int \partial_x^k (q_1^5) (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \right| + \left|\int \partial_x^k (q_1^5) (\partial_x^{k} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' \right| \\ &\leq C \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'} + \frac 1{200}\int (\partial_x^{k} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+\frac 1{200} \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' , \end{align*} and \begin{align*} & \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'} \lesssim \int \left(\partial_x^k (q_1^5)\right)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+ 2 k_1+2k_2+2k_3+2k_4+2k_5+1}\\ & \lesssim \sum_{ \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{2}{k_1+k_2+k_3+k_4+k_5=k}{k_5\geq k_4\geq k_3\geq k_2\geq k_1} } \left( \Pi_{l=1}^3 \| (\partial_x^{k_l} q_1 )^2 {\varphi_{2k_l+2}} \|_{L^\infty} \right) \| (\partial_x^{k_4} q_1 )^2 {\varphi_{2k_4-2}} \|_{L^\infty}\int |\partial_x^{k_5} q_1|^2\varphi'_{\theta_1+2k_5-1} \\ & \lesssim \delta(x_0^{-1})\sum_{k'=0}^k \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}'. \end{align*} where the $L^\infty$ norms above are estimated using \eqref{ply2}. The other terms, all containing $f_0$, are similar and easier.
nodes.statement_short: Nonlinear term bound (ply3)

nodes.name: Close the induction and conclude
nodes.statement: By integration of $F'_k$ using \eqref{ply3} and \eqref{ply2}, we obtain $$ F_{\theta_1,k}(t) + \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$} \\ x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} $$ Arguing as in the proof of \eqref{linfty}, we prove \eqref{ply2} for $k'=k$. The induction argument being complete, we finish the proof as in \eqref{A11}.
nodes.statement_short: Close the induction and conclude

nodes.name: Energy identity for the weighted norm
nodes.statement: We compute from {\rm (\ref{eqofeps})}: \begin{align*} &\frac 12\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2 = \int \varepsilon_s \varepsilon \varphi_{10}\\ &=\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\bigg[\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\Lambda \varepsilon+\left(-\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon - (\varepsilon +pY_0 +Q_b )^5 + Q_b ^5 +p5 Q^4 Y_0\right)_y \\ & - p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4(p-q))_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0+\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b + \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon +pY_0)_y \\ & + \Phi_{{b}} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y\bigg]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Energy identity for the weighted norm

nodes.name: Linear terms
nodes.statement: We integrate by parts the linear term and use $y\varphi_{10}'={10}\varphi_{10}$ for $y\geq 1$ and $\varphi_{10}'''\ll \varphi_{10}'$ for $y$ large enough to derive the bound \begin{eqnarray*} &&\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\left[\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\Lambda \varepsilon+\left(-\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right)_y\right] \\& = & -\frac12\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int y\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2-\frac 32\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon_y^2-\frac12\int\varphi'_{10}\varepsilon^2+\frac 12\int\varphi_{10}'''\varepsilon^2\\ & \leq & -\frac{10}2\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int \varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2-\frac 14\int\varphi_{10}'(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)+C\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Linear terms

nodes.name: Nonlinear term in epsilon
nodes.statement: By integration by parts in the nonlinear term, we can remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$ to obtain (using $|Q_b|+|(Q_b)_y|\leq Ce^{-\frac 12 {y}}$ for $y>0$) \begin{eqnarray*} \left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon \left[(\varepsilon +Q_b )^5 -Q_b ^5\right]_y\right| &\lesssim & \int_{y>0} \varphi_{10}e^{-\frac 12 {y}}\varepsilon^2(|\varepsilon|^3 +1) +\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^6\\ & \lesssim & \int_{y>0} e^{-\frac 14 {y}} \varepsilon^2(|\varepsilon|^3 +1)+\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^6\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Nonlinear term in epsilon

nodes.name: p Y_0 nonlinear terms
nodes.statement: Next, by the bootstrap estimates, \begin{align*} & \left| \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon \left[ (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0)^5 - 5 p Q^4 Y_0 - (\varepsilon+Q_b)^5\right]_y\right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y>10} \varepsilon e^{-\frac 12 y}\left(p^2 + |b||p| + |p| (|\varepsilon|+|\varepsilon|^5 \right) \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: p Y_0 nonlinear terms

nodes.name: p_s term
nodes.statement: By \eqref{BSbsps} and $Y_0 \in \mathcal{Y}$, $$ \left| p_s \int Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right| \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: p_s term

nodes.name: p - q term
nodes.statement: By \eqref{cl.2} and \eqref{BSp}, \begin{align*} & \left| \int 5 (Q^4 (p-q))_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10}\right| =\left| \int 5 (p-q) e^{-4 |y|} (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y \right| \\ &\leq C \frac 1{s^2} \int (|\varepsilon_y|+|\varepsilon|) e^{-|y|}\varphi_{10} \leq \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{10} + C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: p - q term

nodes.name: lambda_s p term
nodes.statement: By \eqref{BSparam}, $$ \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \int \Lambda Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right| \lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: lambda_s p term

nodes.name: Geometrical parameters and Phi_b, Psi_b terms
nodes.statement: The terms involving the geometrical parameters are controlled from the exponential localization of $Q_b$ on the right and {\rm (\ref{BSlsl})}--{\rm (\ref{BSparam})}: $$\left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(\Lambda Q_b)\right|\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$ \begin{align*}\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\right|&\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\left[\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}+\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2\right]\\ &\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}+\delta(\alpha^*) \int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2,\end{align*} $$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Phi_b\right|\lesssim |b_s| \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$ We control similarily the interaction with the error from {\rm (\ref{eq:202})}: $$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Psi_b\right|\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Geometrical parameters and Phi_b, Psi_b terms

nodes.name: Bound on the W term (Wdix)
nodes.statement: Finally, we claim \begin{equation} \left| \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon W_y\right| \leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2} + \frac 1{50} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}' \end{equation} We only treat the first term in $W$, the other terms are similar and easier. First, integrating by parts, we remove the derivative from $\varepsilon$ to obtain derivative on $q$, $\varphi_{10}$. Indeed, \begin{align*} & - \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} = \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right] (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y\\ & =\int \bigg\{\left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5- (Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]_y \\ &- 5(Q_b+pY_0)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] + 20 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \bigg\}q\varphi_{10} \\ &+ 5\int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q\varphi_{10}' \\ & = - \int \left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5-(Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right] (q_y\varphi_{10}+q \varphi_{10}') \\ &- 5\int \left\{(Q_b+pY_0)_y \left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] - 4 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \right\} q\varphi_{10} \\ & + 5 \int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q \varphi_{10}' . \end{align*} From the above expression, we obtain for $s$ large enough (using $\|\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1}\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*)$ and $\|q\|_{L^\infty(y>0)} \lesssim \frac 1s$) \begin{align*} &\left| \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} \right|\\ & \lesssim \int (|q|+|q_y|) e^{-\frac {|y|}2} (|\varepsilon|+|p|+|b|)|\varepsilon| +\int (|q_y|\varphi_{10} + |q|\varphi_{10}') |\varepsilon|^5 \\ & \leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2} + \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'+\delta(\alpha^*)\int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} . \end{align*} To control the last term above, we use $q_y(t,y)=\lambda^{\frac 32} \partial_x q_0(t,\lambda y + x(t)) $ so that $ |q_y(t,y)|\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 32} (\lambda y +x(t))^{-\theta-1} \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}(t) (y+1)^{-1}, $ for $y>10$, and $$ \int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} \lesssim \frac {\lambda^{\frac 12}}{x^{\theta}} \int_{y>0} \varepsilon^2 (y+1)^{-1} \varphi_{10} \leq \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound on the W term (Wdix)

nodes.name: Integrate by parts the first W term
nodes.statement: We only treat the first term in $W$, the other terms are similar and easier. First, integrating by parts, we remove the derivative from $\varepsilon$ to obtain derivative on $q$, $\varphi_{10}$. Indeed, \begin{align*} & - \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} = \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right] (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y\\ & =\int \bigg\{\left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5- (Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]_y \\ &- 5(Q_b+pY_0)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] + 20 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \bigg\}q\varphi_{10} \\ &+ 5\int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q\varphi_{10}' \\ & = - \int \left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5-(Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right] (q_y\varphi_{10}+q \varphi_{10}') \\ &- 5\int \left\{(Q_b+pY_0)_y \left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] - 4 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \right\} q\varphi_{10} \\ & + 5 \int \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 - Q^4 \right] \varepsilon q \varphi_{10}' . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate by parts the first W term

nodes.name: Bound it
nodes.statement: From the above expression, we obtain for $s$ large enough (using $\|\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1}\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*)$ and $\|q\|_{L^\infty(y>0)} \lesssim \frac 1s$) \begin{align*} &\left| \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} \right|\\ & \lesssim \int (|q|+|q_y|) e^{-\frac {|y|}2} (|\varepsilon|+|p|+|b|)|\varepsilon| +\int (|q_y|\varphi_{10} + |q|\varphi_{10}') |\varepsilon|^5 \\ & \leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2} + \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'+\delta(\alpha^*)\int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound it

nodes.name: Control the q_y term by the tail decay
nodes.statement: To control the last term above, we use $q_y(t,y)=\lambda^{\frac 32} \partial_x q_0(t,\lambda y + x(t)) $ so that $ |q_y(t,y)|\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 32} (\lambda y +x(t))^{-\theta-1} \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}(t) (y+1)^{-1}, $ for $y>10$, and $$ \int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} \lesssim \frac {\lambda^{\frac 12}}{x^{\theta}} \int_{y>0} \varepsilon^2 (y+1)^{-1} \varphi_{10} \leq \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'. $$
nodes.statement_short: Control the q_y term by the tail decay

nodes.name: Collect estimates
nodes.statement: The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2+{10}\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$ and {\rm (\ref{keyestimate})} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Collect estimates

nodes.name: Step 1: weighted controls
nodes.statement: {\bf step 1} Weighted $L^2$ controls at the right. We first recall from \cite{MMR1}, proof of Proposition 3.1, the following controls for all $s\in [0,s_0]$, \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}y\varepsilon^2(s)\lesssim \left(1+\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac{10}9}(s)}\right)\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}(s), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}y^2\varepsilon^2(s)\lesssim \left(1+\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac {10}9}(s)}\right)\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}(s), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \int_{y>0}|\varepsilon(s)|\lesssim \mathcal N_2^{\frac{1}{2}}(s). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall weighted L^2 controls from MMR1

nodes.name: Step 2: algebraic computations
nodes.statement: {\bf step 2} Algebraic computations on $\mathcal F_{i}$. First, note that the equation of $\varepsilon$ \eqref{eqofeps} can be rewritten as follows: \begin{align} \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon -\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon - Z\right)_y \\ & -p_s Y_0 +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p Y_0)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} , \end{align} where $$ Z=(Q_b+pY_0+q+ \varepsilon )^5 -Q_b^5 - 5Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5, $$ $$\Phi_b = - {b}_{s} \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P,\quad -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b.$$ We compute \begin{align*} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] &= 2\int \psi_B(\varepsilon_y)_s \varepsilon_y\\ & + 2\int \varepsilon_s \left[ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right]\\ & -2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_s \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \\& + 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon + \frac j s \mathcal F_{i} \end{align*} which we rewrite \begin{equation} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] = f^{(i)}_{1}+f^{(i)}_2+f^{(i)}_3, \end{equation} where {\allowdisplaybreaks \begin{align*} f^{(i)}_{1} &= 2 \int \left( \varepsilon_{s} - {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} {\Lambda} \varepsilon\right) \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ\right) ,\\ f^{(i,j)}_2 &= 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_B Z \right) +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}, \\ f^{(i)}_3 &= - 2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\ &+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon. \end{align*} } We claim the following estimates on the above terms: for some $\mu_0>0$, \begin{align} & \frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{1}\leq - \mu_0 \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}, \\ & \left|\frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{k}\right|\leq \frac {\mu_0}{10} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}+ C s^{10\beta -9}, \quad \hbox{for $k=2,3.$} \end{align} Inserting \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2} into {\rm (\ref{eqfnoneoge})} yields {\rm (\ref{lyapounovconrolbis})} for all $j$. In steps 3 - step 5, we prove \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2}. Observe that the definitions of $\varphi_i$ and $\psi$ imply the following estimates: \begin{align} \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad &|\varphi_i'''(y) | + | \varphi_i''(y) |+|\psi'''(y)|+|y\psi'(y)|+|\psi(y)| \lesssim \varphi'_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i(y),\\ \forall y\in (-\infty,2], \quad & e^{ |y|} \psi(y) + e^{ |y|} \psi'(y) +\varphi_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i'(y),\\ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad & \varphi_2'(y)\lesssim \varphi_1(y) \lesssim \varphi'_2(y). \end{align} In particular, \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim{\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{1}} (s)\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_2} (s),\quad \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi_{1,B} (y) dy\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Algebraic decomposition of d/ds(s^j F_i)

nodes.name: Rewrite the equation of epsilon
nodes.statement: First, note that the equation of $\varepsilon$ \eqref{eqofeps} can be rewritten as follows: \begin{align} \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon -\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon - Z\right)_y \\ & -p_s Y_0 +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p Y_0)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} , \end{align} where $$ Z=(Q_b+pY_0+q+ \varepsilon )^5 -Q_b^5 - 5Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5, $$ $$\Phi_b = - {b}_{s} \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P,\quad -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b.$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the equation of epsilon

nodes.name: Compute d/ds(s^j F_i) = f_1 + f_2 + f_3
nodes.statement: We compute \begin{align*} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] &= 2\int \psi_B(\varepsilon_y)_s \varepsilon_y\\ & + 2\int \varepsilon_s \left[ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right]\\ & -2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_s \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \\& + 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon + \frac j s \mathcal F_{i} \end{align*} which we rewrite \begin{equation} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right] = f^{(i)}_{1}+f^{(i)}_2+f^{(i)}_3, \end{equation} where {\allowdisplaybreaks \begin{align*} f^{(i)}_{1} &= 2 \int \left( \varepsilon_{s} - {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} {\Lambda} \varepsilon\right) \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ\right) ,\\ f^{(i,j)}_2 &= 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_B Z \right) +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}, \\ f^{(i)}_3 &= - 2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\ &+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon. \end{align*} }
nodes.statement_short: Compute d/ds(s^j F_i) = f_1 + f_2 + f_3

nodes.name: Claim (re1), (re2)
nodes.statement: We claim the following estimates on the above terms: for some $\mu_0>0$, \begin{align} & \frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{1}\leq - \mu_0 \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}, \\ & \left|\frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{k}\right|\leq \frac {\mu_0}{10} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} + C s^{-4}+ C s^{10\beta -9}, \quad \hbox{for $k=2,3.$} \end{align} Inserting \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2} into {\rm (\ref{eqfnoneoge})} yields {\rm (\ref{lyapounovconrolbis})} for all $j$. In steps 3 - step 5, we prove \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2}.
nodes.statement_short: Claim (re1), (re2); they imply the Lyapunov control

nodes.name: Properties of the weights
nodes.statement: Observe that the definitions of $\varphi_i$ and $\psi$ imply the following estimates: \begin{align} \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad &|\varphi_i'''(y) | + | \varphi_i''(y) |+|\psi'''(y)|+|y\psi'(y)|+|\psi(y)| \lesssim \varphi'_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i(y),\\ \forall y\in (-\infty,2], \quad & e^{ |y|} \psi(y) + e^{ |y|} \psi'(y) +\varphi_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i'(y),\\ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad & \varphi_2'(y)\lesssim \varphi_1(y) \lesssim \varphi'_2(y). \end{align} In particular, \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim{\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{1}} (s)\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_2} (s),\quad \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi_{1,B} (y) dy\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Properties of the weights

nodes.name: Step 3: control of f_1
nodes.statement: {\bf step 3} Control of $f_1^{(i)}$. Proof of \eqref{re1}. We compute $ f_{1}^{(i)} $ using \eqref{eqebis} \begin{align*} \rm f_{1}^{(i)}& = 2 \int \left( -\varepsilon_{yy} {+} \varepsilon {-}Z \right)_y \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y{+}\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}{-}\psi_BZ \right) \\ & +2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q_b \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z \right) \\ & + 2 \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) \int (Q_b + \varepsilon+pY_0)_y \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Phi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Psi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + \int \left(-p_sY_0 +(5Q^4(p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0\right) \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & = {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,1}}+ {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,2}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,3}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,4}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,5}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,6}}. \end{align*} \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}: We first integrate by parts \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right] \psi_B \\ & + & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). \end{eqnarray*} We compute the various terms : \begin{align*} & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2\\ & =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2 - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\ & -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}. \end{align*} Next after integration by parts: \begin{eqnarray*} & & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\ & & =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\}, \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon = 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\ & = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon \right\}\\ & - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]. \end{eqnarray*} We collect the above computations and obtain the following \begin{align*} & f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\ & -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\ & - 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B' - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^> \end{align*} where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$. We recall \begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim {\delta(\alpha^*)} . \end{equation} $\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}: $$ \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}, $$ $$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ by choosing $B$ large enough. By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small) \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} \\& \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2} \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp} $$ \left(\int q^4 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$, \begin{eqnarray*} && \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}} (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&- 20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \bigg|\\ && \lesssim B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left( |p|^2+|q|^2\right) (|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon| (|p|+|q|) \left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is $$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$ To estimate it, we note the following \begin{align*} &\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\ & \lesssim |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|). \end{align*} Now, using \begin{equation} \int |p| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, \quad \int |q_y| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}, \end{equation} we obtain proceeding as before \begin{align*} &\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon] \right|\\ &\lesssim \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{align*} We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$: \begin{eqnarray*} && \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\ &&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\ && +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\ && \lesssim \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}\\ && \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization (see more details in \cite{MMR1}) \begin{eqnarray*} & & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right| \\ &=& \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon -Z\right) Z \right|\\ & \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\ & \leq & \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}\right] +\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} $\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before. We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate: $$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, to control: \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6 -\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon \right) \varphi_{i,B}' \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6 + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ & \lesssim (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}, \end{align*} \begin{align*} & \Bigg| \int_{y>B/2} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right](Q_b )_y (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) \\ &-20 \int_{y>B/2} Q'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B})\Bigg|\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Since $Y_0\in \mathcal{Y}$, we argue similarly to obtain \begin{align*} &\left| \int (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\ &\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Next, we have from \eqref{BSqy}, \begin{align*} &\left| \int (\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B) q_y \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Also, \begin{align*} \left| \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'\right| = \left| \int Z (\varepsilon_{yy} \psi_B' + \varepsilon_y \psi_B'')\right| \leq \frac 1{100} \int (\varepsilon_{yy}^2 + \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2) \psi_B' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} $\bullet$ In the region $|y|<B/2$, $\varphi_{i,B}(s,y) = 1+ y/B$ and $\psi_B(y)=1$. In particular, $\varphi_{i,B}'''=\psi_B'=0$ in this region, and we obtain: \begin{align*} (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim} & = - \frac {1}{B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \Big\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \\ & + \frac 13 \left( (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0+q)^6 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6 Q_b^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon -6 Z\varepsilon \right) \\ & + 2\left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b )_y \\ & -40 yQ'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ & + 2 y(p Y_0'+q_y)\left((\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right)\Big\} \\ & = - \frac {1} { B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right\} + R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon), \end{align*} where \begin{align*} R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon) = - \frac {1} { B} & \int_{|y|<B/2} \Bigg\{ \frac 13 \bigg( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0 + q)^6 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6Q_b^5 \varepsilon\\ & -30 Q^4 (pY_0+q)\varepsilon - 6Z\varepsilon - 15 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 \bigg)\\ & +2 \left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+ pY_0 + q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5 Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b)_y \\ &- 20 y Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon - 10 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2 \\ & +2 y (pY_0'+q_y) \left( (\varepsilon +Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 +q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right)\Bigg\} \end{align*} As before, we estimate \begin{align*} |R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon)|&\lesssim \int_{|y|<B} \varepsilon^2 \left( \delta(\alpha^*) + |b|+ |p|+|q|\right) + \int_{|y|<B} |\varepsilon| (p^2+ q^2 + b^2) \\&\lesssim \frac 1{100}\int_{|y|<B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result. \begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that if $B\geq B_{0}$, then $$ \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) - \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}. $$ \end{lemma} Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough: $$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim \leq - \frac { \mu_{3}} {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ The collection of above estimates yields the bound: \begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1} \leq - \frac {\mu_4} B \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4}, \end{equation} for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$. \medskip \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,2}$}}: We decompose $f_{1,2}$ in a suitable way: \begin{align*} f^{(i)}_{1,2} & = 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q (L \varepsilon) -2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)\int\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B})\Lambda Q \\ &+ 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P) \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\\ & + 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y -(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \\& + 2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q (Z-5Q^4\varepsilon) \end{align*} Observe from {\rm (\ref{ortho1})}: $$\int \Lambda Q (L\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,L\Lambda Q)=-2(\varepsilon,Q)=0.$$ We now use the orthogonality conditions $( \varepsilon, y {\Lambda} Q)=0$ and the definition of $\varphi_{i,B}$ to estimate: $$ \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| = \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon \left(1-\varphi_{i,B}+ \frac yB\right)\right| \lesssim e^{- \frac B 8 } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} , $$ so that for $B$ large enough: \begin{align*} \left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| &\lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} \right) e^{- \frac B 8} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} For the next term in $f_{1,2}^{(i)}$, we first integrate by parts to remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$. Then, by the properties of $\varphi_{i,B}$, $\psi_B$, $P$ and $\chi_b$ \eqref{eq:210}, we obtain for $\alpha^*$ small, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left| 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P) \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\right|\\ & \lesssim & |b| \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2 \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s) +\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} Next, integrating by parts, using the exponential decay of $Q$ and since $\psi_B(y)\equiv 1$ on $[-\frac B2,\infty)$: \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y -(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \right|\\ & \lesssim & \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2 \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}, \end{eqnarray*} and finally \begin{align*} &\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left[Z-5Q^4\varepsilon\right] \right| \lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) \\ & \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s) +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$ |f^{(i)}_{1,2}|\leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac C{s^4}. $$ \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$}}: Integrating by parts, we claim the identity \begin{align*} & -\frac 16 \int \psi_B' \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6 -Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5\varepsilon - 6Q^5(pY_0+q) -6 Q_b q^5\right]\\ & = \int \psi_B (Q_b)_y Z - 5 \int \psi_B Q' Q^4 \varepsilon + \int (Q_b^5-Q^5)_y \varepsilon\psi_B+ 5\int (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4(pY_0+q) \psi_B \\ &+\int \psi_B p Y_0' Z +\int (Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' \psi_B + 5\int Q^4(pY_0+q) pY_0'\psi_B +\int \psi_B p Y_0' q^5 Q_b\\ & +\int \psi_B q_y \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 -Q^5\right] +\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Z + 5\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4 (pY_0+q). \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,3}& = & \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \bigg\{2\int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\\ & + & 2 \int(Q_b-Q+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\\ & + & \frac 13 \int\psi_B'\left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon-6Q^5(pY_0+q) -6 Q_b q^5\right]\\ & + & 2 \int\varepsilon\psi_B(Q_b^5-Q^5)_y+ 10 \int \psi_B (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4 (pY_0+q)\\ & + & 2 \int \psi_B(Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' +10 \int Q^4 (pY_0+q) pY_0' \psi_B +2 \int \psi_B pY_0' q^5 Q_b\\ & + & 2 \int \psi_Bq_y \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5-Q^5-5Q_b q^4\right] +10\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4(pY_0+q)\bigg\}. \end{eqnarray*} The first term is treated using the cancellation $L Q'=0$ and the orthogonality conditions $(\varepsilon, \Lambda Q)=(\varepsilon,Q)=0$, so that $(yQ',\varepsilon)=0$. Thus, by the definitions of $\varphi_{i,B}$ and $\psi_B$, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\right| \\ &&=\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon\left(1+\frac yB-\varphi_{i,B}\right)\right]\right| \\&& \lesssim \left(\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1{s^2}\right)e^{-\frac B {10}}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} Then, as before, integrating by parts, and using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2b \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int (\chi_bP)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\\ &&\lesssim \frac 1{s} \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right) B^{\frac 12} \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}\leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int \varepsilon_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right| \\ &&\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}\leq \frac1{500} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} \begin{align*} & \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right| \left| \int pY_0' \left[ - \psi_B' \varepsilon_y - \psi_B \varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\ & \lesssim \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right) \frac 1s \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq \frac1{500} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} In conclusion for $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$, on gets $$ |f^{(i)}_{1,3}| \leq \frac1{50} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+ \frac C{s^4}, $$ for $B$ large enough and $\alpha^*$ small enough, $s_0$ large enough. \medskip \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,4}$}}: Recall $$ f^{(i)}_{1,4} = - 2{b}_{s} \int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \left( - \psi_B\varepsilon_{yy} -\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right).$$ We estimate after integrations by parts \begin{eqnarray*} \left| \int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \left( - \psi_B\varepsilon_{y } \right)_y\right|&\lesssim& \int|\varepsilon|\left|(\psi_B ( (\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y) P)_y)_y\right| \\ & \lesssim & B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}. \end{eqnarray*} $$\left|\int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right|\lesssim B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}.$$ The estimate of the nonlinear term follows from {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $\psi\leq (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$: \begin{eqnarray*} && \left|\int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \psi_BZ\right| \lesssim \int\psi_B((|Q_b|^4|+p^4+q^4) \varepsilon|+|\varepsilon|^5 +b^2 + p^2 + q^2)\\ && \lesssim B^{\frac 12}\left( \int (|\varepsilon|^2+ |\varepsilon|^6) \psi_B\right)^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} \lesssim B^{\frac 12} \left(\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \right)^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} . \end{eqnarray*} Together with \eqref{BSparam}, these estimates yield the bound: $$|f_{1,4}| \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.$$ \medskip \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,5}$}}: Recall: $$ f^{(i)}_{1,5}= 2 \int \Psi_b \left( -(\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z \right). $$ We now rely on \eqref{BSbsps} to estimate by integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, $$ \left| \int (\Psi_b)_y \psi_B\varepsilon_{y}\right| \lesssim B^{\frac 12} b^2 \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12} \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}. $$ By \eqref{eq:202} and the exponential decay of $\varphi_{i,B}$ in the left, $$\left| \int \Psi_b \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon\right|\lesssim \left( b^2 B^{\frac 12}+ e^{-\frac 1{2 |b|^{\gamma}}}\right)|b|^{1+\gamma}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +C|b|^{4}.$$ For the nonlinear term, similarly and using \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, \begin{eqnarray*} \left| \int \Psi_b \psi_B Z \right| \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$ | f^{(i)}_{1,5}| \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.$$ \medskip \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,6}$}}: Recall that this term writes \begin{align*} \left| \int \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right) \left( - (\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right) \right| \end{align*} By \eqref{BSbsps}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{BSparam}, \begin{align*} & \left| \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right) \right| +\left| \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)_y \right| \\ & \lesssim e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \left( \frac 1{s^2} + \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \end{align*} and thus $$ | f^{(i)}_{1,6}| \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2} } +\frac 1{s^4}. $$
