nodes.statement: We compute $ f_{1}^{(i)} $ using \eqref{eqebis} \begin{align*} \rm f_{1}^{(i)}& = 2 \int \left( -\varepsilon_{yy} {+} \varepsilon {-}Z \right)_y \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y{+}\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}{-}\psi_BZ \right) \\ & +2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q_b \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z \right) \\ & + 2 \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) \int (Q_b + \varepsilon+pY_0)_y \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Phi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + 2 \int \Psi_{{b}} \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & + \int \left(-p_sY_0 +(5Q^4(p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0\right) \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right) \\ & = {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,1}}+ {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,2}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,3}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,4}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,5}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,6}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split f_1 into six terms

nodes.name: Term f_{1,1}: virial coercivity
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}: We first integrate by parts \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right] \psi_B \\ & + & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). \end{eqnarray*} We compute the various terms : \begin{align*} & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2\\ & =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2 - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\ & -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}. \end{align*} Next after integration by parts: \begin{eqnarray*} & & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\ & & =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\}, \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon = 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\ & = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon \right\}\\ & - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]. \end{eqnarray*} We collect the above computations and obtain the following \begin{align*} & f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\ & -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\ & - 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B' - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^> \end{align*} where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$. We recall \begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim {\delta(\alpha^*)} . \end{equation} $\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}: $$ \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}, $$ $$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ by choosing $B$ large enough. By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small) \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} \\& \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2} \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp} $$ \left(\int q^4 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$, \begin{eqnarray*} && \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}} (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&- 20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \bigg|\\ && \lesssim B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left( |p|^2+|q|^2\right) (|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon| (|p|+|q|) \left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is $$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$ To estimate it, we note the following \begin{align*} &\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\ & \lesssim |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|). \end{align*} Now, using \begin{equation} \int |p| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, \quad \int |q_y| \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}, \end{equation} we obtain proceeding as before \begin{align*} &\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon] \right|\\ &\lesssim \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{align*} We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$: \begin{eqnarray*} && \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\ &&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\ && +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\ && \lesssim \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}\\ && \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization (see more details in \cite{MMR1}) \begin{eqnarray*} & & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right| \\ &=& \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon -Z\right) Z \right|\\ & \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\ & \leq & \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}\right] +\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} $\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before. We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate: $$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, to control: \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6 -\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon \right) \varphi_{i,B}' \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6 + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ & \lesssim (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}, \end{align*} \begin{align*} & \Bigg| \int_{y>B/2} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right](Q_b )_y (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) \\ &-20 \int_{y>B/2} Q'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B})\Bigg|\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Since $Y_0\in \mathcal{Y}$, we argue similarly to obtain \begin{align*} &\left| \int (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\ &\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Next, we have from \eqref{BSqy}, \begin{align*} &\left| \int (\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B) q_y \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Also, \begin{align*} \left| \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'\right| = \left| \int Z (\varepsilon_{yy} \psi_B' + \varepsilon_y \psi_B'')\right| \leq \frac 1{100} \int (\varepsilon_{yy}^2 + \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2) \psi_B' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} $\bullet$ In the region $|y|<B/2$, $\varphi_{i,B}(s,y) = 1+ y/B$ and $\psi_B(y)=1$. In particular, $\varphi_{i,B}'''=\psi_B'=0$ in this region, and we obtain: \begin{align*} (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim} & = - \frac {1}{B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \Big\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \\ & + \frac 13 \left( (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0+q)^6 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6 Q_b^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon -6 Z\varepsilon \right) \\ & + 2\left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b )_y \\ & -40 yQ'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ & + 2 y(p Y_0'+q_y)\left((\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right)\Big\} \\ & = - \frac {1} { B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right\} + R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon), \end{align*} where \begin{align*} R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon) = - \frac {1} { B} & \int_{|y|<B/2} \Bigg\{ \frac 13 \bigg( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0 + q)^6 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6Q_b^5 \varepsilon\\ & -30 Q^4 (pY_0+q)\varepsilon - 6Z\varepsilon - 15 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 \bigg)\\ & +2 \left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+ pY_0 + q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5 Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b)_y \\ &- 20 y Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon - 10 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2 \\ & +2 y (pY_0'+q_y) \left( (\varepsilon +Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 +q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right)\Bigg\} \end{align*} As before, we estimate \begin{align*} |R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon)|&\lesssim \int_{|y|<B} \varepsilon^2 \left( \delta(\alpha^*) + |b|+ |p|+|q|\right) + \int_{|y|<B} |\varepsilon| (p^2+ q^2 + b^2) \\&\lesssim \frac 1{100}\int_{|y|<B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result. \begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that if $B\geq B_{0}$, then $$ \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) - \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}. $$ \end{lemma} Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough: $$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim \leq - \frac { \mu_{3}} {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ The collection of above estimates yields the bound: \begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1} \leq - \frac {\mu_4} B \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4}, \end{equation} for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,1}: virial coercivity

nodes.name: Integrate by parts and split regions
nodes.statement: We first integrate by parts \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right] \psi_B \\ & + & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). \end{eqnarray*} We compute the various terms : \begin{align*} & 2\int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon -Z \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2\\ & =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2 - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\ & -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}. \end{align*} Next after integration by parts: \begin{eqnarray*} & & 2 \int\left[ -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\ & & =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\}, \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon = 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\ & = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon \right\}\\ & - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]. \end{eqnarray*} We collect the above computations and obtain the following \begin{align*} & f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\ & -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\ & - 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\ & - 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\ & + 2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B' - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\ & = (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^> \end{align*} where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate by parts and split regions

nodes.name: Recall Sobolev bound on epsilon
nodes.statement: We recall \begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim {\delta(\alpha^*)} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall Sobolev bound on epsilon

nodes.name: Left region y<-B/2
nodes.statement: $\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}: $$ \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}, $$ $$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ by choosing $B$ large enough. By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small) \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-} {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6} {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} \\& \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2} \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*} where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp} $$ \left(\int q^4 \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$, \begin{eqnarray*} && \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}} (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&- 20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \bigg|\\ && \lesssim B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left( |p|^2+|q|^2\right) (|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\ &&+B \int |\varepsilon| (|p|+|q|) \left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Left region y<-B/2

nodes.name: Right region y>B/2
nodes.statement: $\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before. We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate: $$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim \frac 1 {B^2} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, to control: \begin{align*} & \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6 -\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon \right) \varphi_{i,B}' \right| \\ & \lesssim \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6 + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\ & \lesssim (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\ & \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Right region y>B/2

nodes.name: Middle region: virial quadratic form plus remainder
nodes.statement: $\bullet$ In the region $|y|<B/2$, $\varphi_{i,B}(s,y) = 1+ y/B$ and $\psi_B(y)=1$. In particular, $\varphi_{i,B}'''=\psi_B'=0$ in this region, and we obtain: \begin{align*} (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim} & = - \frac {1}{B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \Big\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \\ & + \frac 13 \left( (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0+q)^6 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6 Q_b^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon -6 Z\varepsilon \right) \\ & + 2\left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b )_y \\ & -40 yQ'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ & + 2 y(p Y_0'+q_y)\left((\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right)\Big\} \\ & = - \frac {1} { B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right\} + R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon), \end{align*} where \begin{align*} R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon) = - \frac {1} { B} & \int_{|y|<B/2} \Bigg\{ \frac 13 \bigg( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0 + q)^6 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6Q_b^5 \varepsilon\\ & -30 Q^4 (pY_0+q)\varepsilon - 6Z\varepsilon - 15 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 \bigg)\\ & +2 \left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+ pY_0 + q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5 Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b)_y \\ &- 20 y Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon - 10 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2 \\ & +2 y (pY_0'+q_y) \left( (\varepsilon +Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 +q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right)\Bigg\} \end{align*} As before, we estimate \begin{align*} |R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon)|&\lesssim \int_{|y|<B} \varepsilon^2 \left( \delta(\alpha^*) + |b|+ |p|+|q|\right) + \int_{|y|<B} |\varepsilon| (p^2+ q^2 + b^2) \\&\lesssim \frac 1{100}\int_{|y|<B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4}, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Middle region: virial quadratic form plus remainder

nodes.name: Localized virial estimate (Lemma B.1)
nodes.statement: We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result. \begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that if $B\geq B_{0}$, then $$ \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) - \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}. $$ \end{lemma}
nodes.statement_short: Localized virial estimate (Lemma B.1)

nodes.name: Bound (eq:cf11) on f_{1,1}
nodes.statement: Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough: $$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim \leq - \frac { \mu_{3}} {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2} \left( \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ The collection of above estimates yields the bound: \begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1} \leq - \frac {\mu_4} B \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4}, \end{equation} for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound (eq:cf11) on f_{1,1}

nodes.name: Term f_{1,2}
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,2}$}}: We decompose $f_{1,2}$ in a suitable way: \begin{align*} f^{(i)}_{1,2} & = 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q (L \varepsilon) -2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)\int\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B})\Lambda Q \\ &+ 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P) \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\\ & + 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y -(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \\& + 2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q (Z-5Q^4\varepsilon) \end{align*} Observe from {\rm (\ref{ortho1})}: $$\int \Lambda Q (L\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,L\Lambda Q)=-2(\varepsilon,Q)=0.$$ We now use the orthogonality conditions $( \varepsilon, y {\Lambda} Q)=0$ and the definition of $\varphi_{i,B}$ to estimate: $$ \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| = \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon \left(1-\varphi_{i,B}+ \frac yB\right)\right| \lesssim e^{- \frac B 8 } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} , $$ so that for $B$ large enough: \begin{align*} \left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| &\lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} \right) e^{- \frac B 8} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \\ & \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} For the next term in $f_{1,2}^{(i)}$, we first integrate by parts to remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$. Then, by the properties of $\varphi_{i,B}$, $\psi_B$, $P$ and $\chi_b$ \eqref{eq:210}, we obtain for $\alpha^*$ small, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left| 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P) \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\right|\\ & \lesssim & |b| \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2 \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s) +\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} Next, integrating by parts, using the exponential decay of $Q$ and since $\psi_B(y)\equiv 1$ on $[-\frac B2,\infty)$: \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y -(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \right|\\ & \lesssim & \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2 \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}, \end{eqnarray*} and finally \begin{align*} &\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q \left[Z-5Q^4\varepsilon\right] \right| \lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) \\ & \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s) +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$ |f^{(i)}_{1,2}|\leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac C{s^4}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,2}

nodes.name: Term f_{1,3}
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$}}: Integrating by parts, we claim the identity \begin{align*} & -\frac 16 \int \psi_B' \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6 -Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5\varepsilon - 6Q^5(pY_0+q) -6 Q_b q^5\right]\\ & = \int \psi_B (Q_b)_y Z - 5 \int \psi_B Q' Q^4 \varepsilon + \int (Q_b^5-Q^5)_y \varepsilon\psi_B+ 5\int (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4(pY_0+q) \psi_B \\ &+\int \psi_B p Y_0' Z +\int (Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' \psi_B + 5\int Q^4(pY_0+q) pY_0'\psi_B +\int \psi_B p Y_0' q^5 Q_b\\ & +\int \psi_B q_y \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 -Q^5\right] +\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Z + 5\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4 (pY_0+q). \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i)}_{1,3}& = & \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \bigg\{2\int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\\ & + & 2 \int(Q_b-Q+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\\ & + & \frac 13 \int\psi_B'\left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon-6Q^5(pY_0+q) -6 Q_b q^5\right]\\ & + & 2 \int\varepsilon\psi_B(Q_b^5-Q^5)_y+ 10 \int \psi_B (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4 (pY_0+q)\\ & + & 2 \int \psi_B(Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' +10 \int Q^4 (pY_0+q) pY_0' \psi_B +2 \int \psi_B pY_0' q^5 Q_b\\ & + & 2 \int \psi_Bq_y \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5-Q^5-5Q_b q^4\right] +10\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4(pY_0+q)\bigg\}. \end{eqnarray*} The first term is treated using the cancellation $L Q'=0$ and the orthogonality conditions $(\varepsilon, \Lambda Q)=(\varepsilon,Q)=0$, so that $(yQ',\varepsilon)=0$. Thus, by the definitions of $\varphi_{i,B}$ and $\psi_B$, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\right| \\ &&=\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon\left(1+\frac yB-\varphi_{i,B}\right)\right]\right| \\&& \lesssim \left(\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1{s^2}\right)e^{-\frac B {10}}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} Then, as before, integrating by parts, and using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2b \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int (\chi_bP)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\\ &&\lesssim \frac 1{s} \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right) B^{\frac 12} \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}\leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} \begin{eqnarray*} &&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int \varepsilon_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right| \\ &&\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}\leq \frac1{500} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} \begin{align*} & \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right| \left| \int pY_0' \left[ - \psi_B' \varepsilon_y - \psi_B \varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\ & \lesssim \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right) \frac 1s \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq \frac1{500} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} In conclusion for $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$, on gets $$ |f^{(i)}_{1,3}| \leq \frac1{50} \frac {\mu_4}{B}\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+ \frac C{s^4}, $$ for $B$ large enough and $\alpha^*$ small enough, $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,3}

nodes.name: Term f_{1,4}
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,4}$}}: Recall $$ f^{(i)}_{1,4} = - 2{b}_{s} \int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \left( - \psi_B\varepsilon_{yy} -\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ \right).$$ We estimate after integrations by parts \begin{eqnarray*} \left| \int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \left( - \psi_B\varepsilon_{y } \right)_y\right|&\lesssim& \int|\varepsilon|\left|(\psi_B ( (\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y) P)_y)_y\right| \\ & \lesssim & B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}. \end{eqnarray*} $$\left|\int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right|\lesssim B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}.$$ The estimate of the nonlinear term follows from {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $\psi\leq (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$: \begin{eqnarray*} && \left|\int \left(\chi_b + \gamma y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \psi_BZ\right| \lesssim \int\psi_B((|Q_b|^4|+p^4+q^4) \varepsilon|+|\varepsilon|^5 +b^2 + p^2 + q^2)\\ && \lesssim B^{\frac 12}\left( \int (|\varepsilon|^2+ |\varepsilon|^6) \psi_B\right)^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} \lesssim B^{\frac 12} \left(\int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \right)^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2} . \end{eqnarray*} Together with \eqref{BSparam}, these estimates yield the bound: $$|f_{1,4}| \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,4}

nodes.name: Term f_{1,5}
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,5}$}}: Recall: $$ f^{(i)}_{1,5}= 2 \int \Psi_b \left( -(\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z \right). $$ We now rely on \eqref{BSbsps} to estimate by integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, $$ \left| \int (\Psi_b)_y \psi_B\varepsilon_{y}\right| \lesssim B^{\frac 12} b^2 \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12} \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}. $$ By \eqref{eq:202} and the exponential decay of $\varphi_{i,B}$ in the left, $$\left| \int \Psi_b \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon\right|\lesssim \left( b^2 B^{\frac 12}+ e^{-\frac 1{2 |b|^{\gamma}}}\right)|b|^{1+\gamma}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +C|b|^{4}.$$ For the nonlinear term, similarly and using \eqref{nonlinearsobolev}, \begin{eqnarray*} \left| \int \Psi_b \psi_B Z \right| \leq \frac 1 {500} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}. \end{eqnarray*} The collection of above estimates yields the bound: $$ | f^{(i)}_{1,5}| \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,5}

nodes.name: Term f_{1,6}
nodes.statement: \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,6}$}}: Recall that this term writes \begin{align*} \left| \int \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right) \left( - (\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right) \right| \end{align*} By \eqref{BSbsps}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{BSparam}, \begin{align*} & \left| \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right) \right| +\left| \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)_y \right| \\ & \lesssim e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \left( \frac 1{s^2} + \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \end{align*} and thus $$ | f^{(i)}_{1,6}| \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2} } +\frac 1{s^4}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Term f_{1,6}

nodes.name: Step 4: f_2 term
nodes.statement: {\bf step 4} $f_2^{(i,j)}$ term. Recall: \begin{eqnarray*} f^{(i,j)}_2 &= & 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ \right)+\frac js\mathcal F_{i}. \end{eqnarray*} We integrate by parts to compute: \begin{align*} & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon (\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_{y} = -\int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B + \frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B',\\ & \int ({\Lambda} \varepsilon ) \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} =- \frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2 y\varphi_{i,B}',\\ & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon\psi_BZ = \int \left( \frac \varepsilon 2 + y\varepsilon_y\right) \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 -5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\ & = \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 -5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\ & - \int (y\psi_B)_y \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6 - \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6 - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\&\qquad - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\ & - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\ & - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\ &+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\ & - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right]. \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} & f^{(i,j)}_2 = 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \bigg\{ \int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B -\frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B' - \frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2 y\varphi_{i,B}' \\& + \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 -5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\ & - \int (y\psi_B)_y \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6 - \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6 - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\ & \qquad - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\ & - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\ & - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\ &+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\ & - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right]\bigg\} +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}. \end{align*} For $y<-B$, we use the exponential decay of $\psi_B, \varphi_{i,B}$ and {\rm (\ref{defphi4})} to estimate: \begin{eqnarray*} &&\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\psi_B+|y|\psi'_B+\varphi_{i,B})(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +|y|\varphi'_{i,B} \varepsilon^2\\ && \lesssim \int_{y<-\frac B2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|\varphi'_{i,B}\varepsilon^2\\ &&\lesssim \int \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} + \left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{1}{100}}\left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{99}{100}} \\ && \lesssim \int \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}}, \end{eqnarray*} where we have used $\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\leq \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2\leq \delta(\alpha^*)$. Together with similar estimates for the other terms, this yields the bound: $$|(f_2^{(i,j)})^<|\lesssim (\frac 1s+\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12})\left(\int \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}}+\frac 1{s^4}\right)\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B} + \frac 1{s^4}.$$ The middle term $f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ is also estimated as follows $$ |f_{2}^{(i,j)}|\leq \delta(\alpha^*) \int ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2) \varphi'_{i,B} + \frac 1{s^4}. $$ It only remains to estimate $(f_{2}^{(i,j)})^>$. Most terms in $(f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ are easily estimated similarly as before. We focus on the following two delicate terms (because of weight at $+\infty$): $$\int_{y> \frac B2} \varepsilon^2 y\varphi_{i,B}', \quad \frac j{s} \int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}.$$ The function $\psi_B$ being bounded, the other terms are easier. First, using \eqref{weightedonebis}, \begin{align*} \frac 1 s\int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} & \lesssim \frac 1s \left( 1+ \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac {10}9}}\right) \mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}\\ & \lesssim s^{\frac {10}9 \beta -1}\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89} \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4}{B} \mathcal N_{2, \rm loc} + s^{10 \beta -9}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Control of f_2

nodes.name: Step 5: f_3 term
nodes.statement: {\bf step 5} $f_3^{(i)}$ term. \begin{align*} f_3^{(i)}&= 2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\ & - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\ &+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon. \end{align*} First, $$ |(Q_b)_s|=\left|b_s P \left( \chi(|b|^{\gamma} y) + \gamma |b|^\gamma y \chi'(|b|^{\gamma} y)\right)\right|\lesssim |b_s| . $$ \begin{align*} &\left| \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\right| \\ & \lesssim |b_s|\int\psi_B \left(\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3+\delta(\alpha^*)) +|\varepsilon| (e^{-\frac {|y|}2} p^4+q^4) \right)\\ & \lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2} + \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}\right) \left( \int (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) \psi_{B} + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 \psi_B \right)^{\frac 12 } \left( \int q^8\psi_B \right)^{\frac 12}\right)\\ & \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} For the next two terms, we first remark that by explicit computations: $$ \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s)^2\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}. $$ Thus, as before, \begin{align*} & \left|\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \right| \\ & \lesssim \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}. \end{align*} Finally, $$ \left| \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon \right| \lesssim \left( \int \psi_B (q_s q^4)^2 \right)^{\frac 12} \left( \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}\lesssim \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^4}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Control of f_3

nodes.name: Step 6: coercivity
nodes.statement: {\bf step 6} Proof of {\rm (\ref{lowerbound})}. We proceed as in \cite{MMR1}. Recall that for $B$ large enough, $\mu>0$, $$\int \psi_B\varepsilon_y^2 + \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon^2- 5 \psi_B Q^4\varepsilon^2 \geq \mu \mathcal N_i.$$ We only have to estimate the error term as follows. For $s_0$ large enough, and $\alpha^*$ small enough, \begin{align*} & \left| \int \left( (Q_b{+}\varepsilon{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} 6 \varepsilon (Q_b^5 {+} q^5 {+} 5 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)) {-} 6 Q^4 \varepsilon^2\right) \psi_B\right| \\ & \lesssim \frac 1 {s^2}\left( \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1s \int \psi_B \varepsilon^2 \leq \frac \mu {10} \mathcal N_i+ \frac 1 {s^4} . \end{align*} This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{propasymtp}.
nodes.statement_short: Coercivity of F_i as in MMR1
